abstract: The rising geopolitical fragmentation, driven by geopolitical tensions, conflicts and wars, has reshaped the global energy landscape, increasing uncertainty and vulnerability in energy markets. These disruptions present serious challenges for different economies in the Global South, where countries already face significant difficulties in facilitating energy transition and mitigating energy poverty. In this context, South-South cooperation may represent an important tool to address energy challenges, particularly through foreign investment. This study investigates the contribution of Chinese FDI to reducing energy poverty in Africa through different channels and whether conflict conditions influence the extent to which Chinese FDI contributes to improving energy outcomes. Our study contributes to the literature on the role of Chinese foreign capital in reducing energy poverty in Africa by examining both the underlying mechanisms and the potential role of conflict conditions in shaping these effects. To empirically explore this complex nexus, we rely on Structural Equation Modelling using a set of energy and socioeconomic variables from 2005 to 2022. The findings reveal a significant positive association between Chinese FDI and energy performance, with the prosperity channel representing the main mechanism. This association appears weaker in conflict-affected contexts, suggesting that geopolitical stability conditions the extent to which foreign investment is associated with improved energy outcomes. Policymakers in the region should consider creating a more attractive and stable investment environment to promote trade ties with Chinese companies, as these ties could be used as a tool to alleviate energy poverty.

title: An optimized PanFlu-IOA-based mRNA vaccine targeting hemagglutinin confers broad-spectrum protection against heterosubtypic influenza viruses in mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The rapid mutation rate of influenza viruses necessitates annual updates of vaccine formulations, underscoring the urgent need for a universal influenza vaccine. Current computationally optimized antigen strategies are mostly confined to certain subtypes and thus fail to elicit broad-spectrum immunity against heterosubtypic strains. Here, we developed the PanFlu-IOA (Pan-Influenza Iteratively Optimized Antigen) toolkit to overcome systemic bias and extract universal antigenic features across diverse evolutionary branches. Using this toolkit, we generated two universal hemagglutinin (HA) sequences G1-HA and G2-HA for influenza virus Group 1 and Group 2, respectively. These two HAs were incorporated into an mRNA-lipid nanoparticle system to construct a broad-spectrum vaccine candidate termed panFluA. In mice, panFluA elicits robust cross-reactive humoral immunity, Th1-biased systemic CD4⁺ T cell responses, and cytotoxic CD8⁺ T cell activation, while successfully establishing durable lung-resident memory T cells. Notably, panFluA conferred potent cross-protection against lethal challenges with highly divergent Group 1 and Group 2 influenza viruses. Mechanistic studies revealed that this protection was mediated by the coordinated action of humoral and cellular immunity, as confirmed by T-cell depletion and passive serum transfer experiments. Overall, panFluA induced broad immune responses against conserved HA antigens. Our study provides a general strategy for next-generation universal influlenza vaccines.

title: Materials Control of Nitric Oxide in Cancer Immunotherapy
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Nitric oxide (NO) can suppress antitumor immunity, support tumor adaptation, or promote immune‐mediated killing, making its therapeutic manipulation highly dependent on exposure. This Review examines how materials control NO source, localization, release kinetics, and chemical fate in cancer immunotherapy, with particular attention to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB). We analyze polymeric donors, nanocarriers, injectable depots, and strategies for restricting endogenous NO production, linking their physicochemical properties to target exposure and immune function. Evidence from checkpoint‐treated models is distinguished from mechanisms established with other therapies and from human associations. Comparative analyses separate donor capacity from measured NO exposure, carrier accumulation from cellular delivery, and distant‐tumor control from demonstrated immune memory. Four overlapping endogenous contexts, comprising tumor adaptation, myeloid suppression, vascular dysfunction, and inflammatory effector activity, guide intervention design without constituting validated patient categories. We identify testable predictions concerning cellular selectivity, release kinetics, and spatial pharmacodynamic responses. Translation requires measurements that connect material behavior to a defined NO‐dependent process while demonstrating preservation of beneficial endothelial and immune functions. This framework provides a basis for evaluating when localized NO delivery or selective inhibition may support ICB, while recognizing the limits of current preclinical and clinical evidence.

title: Non‐Precious Metal High‐Entropy Oxide Sub‐1 nm Nanowires for Li‐O2 Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Highly active and structurally robust cathode catalysts are critically required to boost the electrochemical performance of lithium‐oxygen batteries (LOBs). Herein, a generally synthetic method of non‐precious metal high‐entropy oxide‐polyoxometalate sub‐1 nm nanowires (NPMHEO‐POM SNWs) has been successfully developed induced by POM clusters under mild solvothermal conditions. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations reveal that the dominantly driving forces for the assembly of POMs and multi‐metal oxides are the Coulomb and van der Waals forces, enabling precise theoretical guidance for targeted material synthesis. Benefiting from the 1D ultrafine structure with fully exposed active sites, the precise adjustment of components optimizing the adsorption capability of intermediate (LiO 2 *) and discharge product (Li 2 O 2 ), and the strong interactions of multi‐metal oxides and POMs contributing to the stability, the BiVZrNiCeO x ‐phosphomolybdic acid SNWs‐based LOB achieves a highly specific capacity of 9944 mAh g −1 and stable cycling durability for 312 cycles at 500 mA g −1 , highlighting their great promise as high‐efficiency electrocatalysts for advanced LOBs.

title: Ultra‐Stable Phosphide Barrier Layer for Thermoelectric Bismuth Telluride
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The long‐term reliability of bismuth telluride (BT) thermoelectric power generation devices is severely constrained by the lack of reliable barrier layers. In this work, Ni 2 P is proposed as an ultra‐stable barrier layer for N‐type BT (N–BT). The low thermodynamic driving force for interfacial reaction and the sluggish Ni migration in Ni 2 P together ensure the favorable chemical inertness of the Ni 2 P/N–BT interface, while atomic‐scale bonding endows the interface with high bonding energy, leading to the lowest interfacial contact resistivity (∼1 µΩ cm 2 ), highest bonding strength (∼20 MPa), and longest verified stable duration at 523 K (90 days) among reported barrier layer systems. The resulting seven‐pair BT thermoelectric device achieves a maximum energy conversion efficiency of 6.9% at a temperature difference of 230 K. This work not only addresses the long‐standing bottleneck in power generation applications of BT‐based devices since the 1950s, but also provides guidance for barrier layer design in other thermoelectric systems.

title: Topological Superlattice Stabilized Layered Oxide Cathodes With Sustainable Anionic Redox
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Harnessing the oxygen anionic redox (OAR) at high voltage is envisaged as a fascinating approach to promote the energy density of rechargeable batteries. However, the layered transition metal (TM) oxide cathode materials with OAR activity suffer severely from detrimental phase transformations and local structural disorders, leading to electrochemical performance degradation. Herein, we propose a topological superlattice regulation strategy to construct a cathode material with the Li/Mg/Ni‐triple‐center honeycomb superlattice for sodium‐ion batteries. The combined theoretical and in/ex situ investigations demonstrate that the Li/Mg‐centered superlattice topology activates the OAR reaction to boost specific capacity, while the Ni‐centered honeycomb motif prevents the lattice oxygen release by increasing the TM−O covalency. Furthermore, the multi‐topology superlattice configuration suppresses the P−O phase transition and Li/TM interlayer/intralayer migration to reinforce the honeycomb superstructure stability, improving the oxygen redox reversibility. Consequently, the topological superlattice‐stabilized cathode delivers a high capacity of 242 mAh g −1 and exhibits outstanding cycling stability (91.8% capacity retention after 100 cycles). This work provides new insights into the superstructure regulation of state‐of‐the‐art cathode materials for sustainable batteries.

title: Quicklime Slaking‐Mediated Exothermic Reactions in Polidocanol‐Integrated Ablators with Inhibited Heat Diffusion Enable Cancer Thermal Ablation
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Despite showing a wide application in tumor therapy, the clinically‐used exogenous thermal ablation still suffers from uncontrollable temperature field with rapid heat diffusion. Here an endogenous trigger‐encouraged thermal ablation, namely exothermic reaction‐based thermal ablation (ERTA) based on quicklime slaking and acid‐base neutralization reactions, has been established, wherein CaO nanoparticles were encapsulated with Ag nanoparticles by liposomes to construct ERTA ablators. CaO consumes H 2 O and H + after exothermic reactions to give birth to Ca 2+ and heat. Liposome shell prolongs ERTA via limiting the exothermic reaction rate, and intracellular Ca 2+ overload unites with Ag nanoparticles to produce antitumor ROS to boost cancer ERTA. Importantly, polidocanol‐based foam sclerosing agent (PFSA) with low heat conductivity was integrated to inhibit heat diffusion and confine heat in tumor to elevate temperature and enhance ERTA efficiency. Additionally, PFSA as a routine clinical embolism agent destroys intratumoral blood vessels to occlude blood vessels and establish starvation therapy, which further improves PFSA‐enhanced ERTA efficiency. Consequently, such ERTA‐based ablators and PFSA‐integrated ones outperform the scale‐matched microwave ablation and laboratory‐in photothermal ablation in repressing subcutaneous and orthotopic hepatocellular carcinoma, and orthotopic pancreatic cancer. This endogenous trigger‐activated thermal ablation method provides distinctive insights into thermal ablation, presenting a new thermal ablation protocol.

title: An In Situ Amorphous Thermoconversion Strategy for Macroscopic Glass Heterojunctions
abstract: ABSTRACT Heterojunction fabrication has long been constrained by the stringent lattice‐matching requirements between dissimilar components, limiting the accessible material combinations and processing routes. Here, we report an amorphous thermoconversion strategy for constructing hybrid glass heterojunctions in situ. In this approach, structural competition among liquid phases derived from distinct metal–organic hybrid halide crystal structures generates divergent luminescence across amorphous phases, giving rise to a new family of halide glass heterojunctions. These hybrid halide glasses display excitation‐dependent and time‐gated persistent luminescence that is color‐tunable across a 160 nm wavelength window, a property that enables direct optical visualization and confers broad photonic versatility. Beyond their optical attributes, the resulting macroscopic glass heterojunctions exhibit well‐defined mechanical rigidity and arbitrary processability, supporting spatially resolved fluorescence and persistent luminescence outputs alongside one‐dimensional (1D) optical waveguiding at losses that surpass those of state‐of‐the‐art crystalline counterparts. Therefore, this work delivers the demonstration of macroscopic heterojunctions in halide supramolecular glasses and establishes a scalable route to multi‐channel, low‐dimensional optical waveguide for information storage and encryption applications.

title: Anionic Lone‐Pair‐Like Electrons Induced Ultra‐Low Lattice Thermal Conductivity and High Thermoelectric Performance
abstract: ABSTRACT The traditional lone‐pair electron strategy primarily reduces lattice thermal conductivity ( κ L ) by enhancing anharmonic lattice vibrations. However, this mechanism has long been considered to exist only in specific cations with ns 2 electron configurations (e.g. Sb 3+ , Bi 3+ ), severely restricting the broader applicability of this lone‐pair‐based approach. In this study, CuInSnSe 4 is successfully synthesized via atomic cross‐substitution from the diamondoid CuInSe 2 , wherein the Se atoms exhibit an anionic lone‐pair‐like electronic behavior, revealing a new approach to reducing κ L that differs from conventional cation‐based mechanisms. In contrast to the traditional mechanism that relies on cations to enhance lattice anharmonicity, the anionic lone‐pair electrons weaken the Se‐Se interactions, flatten the optical phonon branches, and consequently significantly expand the scattering phase space, providing more scattering channels for phonons. This anionic lone‐pair electron strategy reduces the room‐temperature κ L from 4.48 to 1.26 W m −1 K −1 . Ultimately, the predicted optimal thermoelectric figure of merit ( ZT ) for p‐type and n‐type CuInSnSe 4 attains values of 1.99 and 0.79, respectively. This work systematically expands the conventional application boundaries of the lone‐pair electron strategy and elucidates a fundamentally distinct mechanism for κ L reduction, providing a new theoretical basis for designing and developing novel high‐efficiency thermoelectric materials with intrinsically low κ L .

title: Revisiting the Role of Dynamic Linkages in Polymer Compatibilization Using Diazirine–Anhydride Conjugates
abstract: ABSTRACT Small‐molecule crosslinkers can compatibilize mixed plastics through reactive extrusion, providing a potential solution to extant challenges in polymer recycling. Existing studies have prioritized the use of crosslinker molecules that incorporate dynamic linkages between reactive warheads; however, the absolute requirement for these dynamic groups remains unproven, and previous comparisons of static versus dynamic crosslinkers employed molecules with vastly different C–H insertion efficiencies. In this study, we employed chemistry‐explicit reaction molecular dynamics simulations, small‐molecule surrogates of interface reactions, phase morphology studies, and mechanical analysis to explicitly test hypotheses around the value of dynamic linkages. Using rationally designed, reactivity‐matched pairs of dynamic and static crosslinkers, we found the presence of dynamic anhydride linkages did not generally improve compatibilization efficacy. Instead, dynamic exchange enabled reorganization of compatibilizing hetero‐crosslinks into non‐compatibilizing homo‐crosslinks over time, while facilitating other undesirable reactivity pathways. Our findings indicate compatibilization performance is dictated by physicochemical control over crosslinker distribution, rather than dynamic bonding, and that the kinetics of dynamic exchange must be tightly regulated to avoid undermining compatibilization. We anticipate that these findings will guide the development of improved crosslinker reagents for polymer compatibilization and other materials applications.

title: One Carbon Matters: Conformational Bending Stabilizes Ferroelectric Nematic Order and Enables Domain‐Modulated Antiferroelectric Smectic C Order
abstract: ABSTRACT Molecular design of ferroelectric nematics has primarily focused on optimizing highly polar rigid mesogenic cores, whereas the role of flexible aliphatic segments in regulating molecular conformation and polar ordering remains insufficiently understood. Here, we show that exchanging the positions of a methylene group and the ether oxygen within the linkage between a polar rigid core and an aliphatic tail (Ar‐O‐CH 2 ‐ versus Ar‐CH 2 ‐O‐) reshapes the molecular conformational landscape and profoundly influences the stability of the ferroelectric nematic (N F ) phase. Molecules with a stronger preference for bent, pear‐like effective geometries exhibit significantly enhanced N F stability, accompanied by reduced splay and bend elastic constants in the apolar nematic phase, and lower apparent activation barriers for dipolar reorientation. Further elongation of the flexible segment introduces competing packing motifs and gives rise to a domain‐modulated antiferroelectric smectic C (SmC AF ) phase. These findings establish conformational bending as a molecular‐shape parameter for controlling hierarchical ferroelectric and antiferroelectric liquid‐crystalline order, bridging the design principles of conventional bent‐core layered ferroelectrics with emerging rod‐like fluid ferroelectric materials.

title: Photo‐Induced Multi‐Physical Field Synergy for Direct Natural Seawater Electrolysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Direct natural seawater electrolysis offers a sustainable route for green hydrogen production, yet severe performance degradation stemming from irreversible interfacial precipitation hinders its practical application. Herein, a photo‐induced multi‐physical field synergy strategy is developed to dynamically regulate interfacial OH − transfer and eliminate cathode pH self‐amplifying polarization. A plasmonic photo‐responsive electrode constructed via ultrathin amorphous MoO 3 coating on PtMo alloy nanoparticles is fabricated to integrate photo‐induced asymmetric electric field (PAEF) and localized photothermal field (PLPF). Such a well‐designed core‐shell structure delivers a record‐high industrial current density of 8 A cm −2 at low overpotential (433 mV) in alkaline seawater. In situ characterizations and spectroscopic analyses verify that the dual fields optimize the electric double‐layer ion distribution and drive microscale thermal convection, accelerating OH − dissipation. Benefiting from the above, the engineered light‐responsive catalytic system exhibits a low overpotential of 232 mV at 100 mA cm −2 in natural seawater, alongside anti‐precipitation ability, and maintains stable operation over 100 h (6.2% decay). A photo‐assisted asymmetric electrolyzer achieves a low cell voltage of 2.27 V at 0.5 A cm −2 for seawater splitting, which realizes effective green hydrogen generation under fluctuating natural solar light (normalized ramp‐following ratio > 0.9).

title: A Phosphonium Relay for Integrated Cleavage‐to‐Cyclization of Cyclic Peptides
abstract: ABSTRACT Head‐to‐tail macrocyclization of peptides is typically performed through stepwise workflows that separate resin cleavage, isolation of linear intermediates, and subsequent cyclization, largely due to incompatible activation requirements for each transformation. Here we report a phosphonium‐mediated relay that unifies these steps within a single activation node. In this design, an electrophile‐activated phosphonium species promotes cleavage from standard 2‐chlorotrityl chloride (2‐CTC) resin and is proposed to enable in situ formation of a C ‐terminally activated intermediate for intramolecular amidation. The strategy directly couples cleavage to cyclization on standard peptide supports without auxiliary linkers, intermediate purification, or high‐dilution cyclization conditions. The method is compatible with diverse peptide sequccnces and functional handles and can be integrated into a closed‐loop automated workflow for end‐to‐end synthesis, with advantages for hydrophobic substrates by avoiding isolation of poorly soluble linear intermediates such as Vespid chemotactic peptide 5f . Process‐level benchmarking against side‐chain anchoring further demonstrated favorable process metrics and gram‐scale scalability. This work establishes a linker‐free cleavage‐to‐cyclization strategy and provides a practical framework for integrated and automation‐compatible cyclic peptide synthesis.

title: Robust Tetrazine‐Bridged Binuclear Iridium(III) Complex Featuring Tunable Conformational Dynamics for Efficient Photothermal Conversion
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing near‐infrared photothermal materials with outstanding conversion efficiency and high photostability remains a critical challenge for small‐molecule systems. We report a unique donor‐acceptor platform based on a binuclear iridium(III) architecture featuring a bridging electron‐deficient 1,2,4,5‐tetrazine ligand. The complex exhibits strong and broad absorption up to 1200 nm in solution and 1500 nm in the solid state, significantly outperforming other metal complexes. Temperature‐ and solvent‐dependent 1 H NMR coupled with X‐ray diffraction suggest the ‘butterfly‐like’ conformational behavior of the complex, while theoretical calculations identify low‐energy charge‐transfer transitions from cyclometalated cores to the tetrazine moiety as the origin of the exceptionally high absorbance and efficient non‐radiative relaxation. This facilitates robust photothermal activity across three different excitation wavelengths (635, 808, 980 nm), delivering an excellent conversion efficiency of 94.9% at 808 nm (acetone solvate) along with long‐term stability over multiple cycles (CHCl 3 /CH 2 Cl 2 ‐derived phase), uniquely tunable through crystal packing engineering. When applied to cellulose paper, the complex drives solar‐to‐thermal water evaporation with an efficiency of 86.6%. This high performance is accompanied by exceptional photostability under prolonged irradiation, ranking the developed material among the most competitive systems reported. Overall, this work establishes bridging 1,2,4,5‐tetrazines and crystal engineering as powerful tools for designing high‐performance organometallic photothermal materials.

title: Photocatalytic Disruption of Concurrent Redox Axes Elicits Convergent Redox Collapse
abstract: ABSTRACT The interconnected antioxidant systems of cancer cells, centered on the glutathione and thioredoxin axes, constitute a promising therapeutic vulnerability. However, simultaneous disruption of both axes by dual‐inhibitor regimens is hampered by pharmacokinetic asynchrony. Herein, we report squaraine‐based photocatalysts as a single‐agent modality that concurrently disrupts these interconnected antioxidant systems in cancer cells. Upon 635 nm light irradiation, IITC depletes intracellular NADPH and GSH through photocatalytic oxidation coupled with type I/II photosensitization. NADPH depletion deprives the reductive coenzyme of thioredoxin reductase in the thioredoxin axis, while glutathione oxidation collapses the central antioxidant axis. Consequently, IITC ablates both antioxidant axes concurrently and exerts potent phototherapeutic anticancer activity in vitro and in vivo. Importantly, during phototherapy IITC undergoes self‐immolation into nontoxic degraded fragments, thereby avoiding phototoxicity post‐treatment. This self‐eliminating, metabolism‐targeted photocatalytic strategy establishes a new avenue for safe and efficient cancer phototherapy.

title: Spatial Electrostatic Complementarity in MOF Pores Enables Selective Recognition of Closely Related Fluoromethanes
abstract: ABSTRACT Trace purification of chemically similar gases is particularly challenging when molecular size and kinetics offer little contrast and conventional affinity descriptors provide conflicting guidance. Trifluoromethane (CHF 3 ) removal from monofluoromethane (CH 3 F) exemplifies this problem: CH 3 F has the greater dipole moment, and CHF 3 is more polarizable. Here, to our knowledge, we report the first adsorptive removal of trace CHF 3 from CH 3 F and demonstrate electrostatic complementary recognition (ECR) in interpenetrated anion‐pillared MOF pores. Localized, directional negative‐potential sites from TiF 6 2– pillars and surrounding electropositive pyridyl C─H domains complement the 1H/3F electrostatic pattern of CHF 3 while geometrically frustrating the inverse 3H/1F pattern of CH 3 F. All other benchmark adsorbents showed an overall preference for CH 3 F, whereas both TIFSIX frameworks achieved a reversal of adsorption preference toward CHF 3 under trace‐relevant conditions. TIFSIX‐Cu‐dpt, featuring a more focused and directional ECR environment, adsorbed 18.5 cm 3 /g of CHF 3 at 0.1 kPa. Neutron diffraction, adsorption thermodynamics, and molecular simulations support a spatially complementary multipoint binding mode. Fixed‐bed breakthrough of a binary feed containing 1000 ppm CHF 3 produced CH 3 F with >99.999% purity relative to CHF 3 at 320 L/kg. These results show how spatial electrostatic complementarity can translate subtle molecular differences beyond conventional scalar descriptors into selective adsorption.

title: Trigonal Prismatic Coordination Field‐Induced d‐Orbital Splitting Enables σ Electron Activation for Efficient Polysulfide Conversion in Li–S Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the electron‐transfer pathways and the mechanism in facilitating polysulfide conversion is crucial for the rational design of catalysts in lithium–sulfur batteries. Herein, we designed an NbSe 2 model catalyst to investigate the electron‐transfer pathways at sublayer transition metal cation sites through coordination field modulation, and revealed the relationship between electron transfer and catalytic efficiency. Moreover, the σ *– σ and π *– σ electron transfer channels at transition metal sites are identified in terms of the coordination field theory and hybrid orbital theory, where the σ *– σ channel exhibits higher electron transfer efficiency and therefore enhances the adsorption and conversion role of transition metal sites in polysulfides. The designed trigonal prismatic NbSe 2 exhibits a reversible capacity up to 799 mAh g −1 at a high rate of 5 C, and the battery maintains stability under ultra‐high sulfur loading, achieving a capacity retention rate as high as 95.85%. From an electronic perspective, this work reveals the role of coordination fields on catalytic activity, providing new insights for the rational design of catalysts in metal–S batteries.

title: Bone Marrow-Targeted Nano-delivery Systems for Refractory Hematologic Malignancies: From Delivery Barriers to Clinical Translation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Hematologic malignancies (HMs) pose a serious threat to human health and are associated with a high metastatic rate and poor prognosis. The strong tumor heterogeneity, marked therapeutic resistance, poor targeting of conventional therapies, and toxic side effects make them a major challenge in the clinical treatment of HMs. As the principal site of hematopoiesis and immune cell production, the bone marrow (BM) is a critical site in the treatment of HMs. However, low blood perfusion and the complexity of the microenvironment severely hinder drug accumulation within the BM, which is also the core bottleneck in the treatment of HMs. Owing to their unique physicochemical properties, nano-delivery systems enable efficient BM-targeted delivery, providing effective strategies to overcome this therapeutic bottleneck. This review discusses the structure of the BM and the mechanisms of delivery barriers, systematically analyzes the design advances of BM-targeted nano-delivery systems, highlights different delivery strategies, and addresses key issues in the clinical translation of nano-delivery systems, including biosafety, manufacturing, and regulation of in vivo delivery efficiency. It also outlines future directions, establishing a BM-targeted delivery framework to advance the treatment of HMs and providing a theoretical reference for the development and clinical application of BM-targeted nano-delivery systems, thereby facilitating breakthroughs in precision therapy for HMs.

title: Orientation-Controlled In-Material Physical Reservoirs Based on Polymer-Wrapped Carbon Nanotube Nanofilms
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Semiconducting polymer poly(m-phenylenevinylene-co-2,5-dioctoxy-p-phenylenevinylene) (PmPV)-wrapped single-walled carbon nanotube (SWCNT–PmPV) nanofilms were fabricated using the Langmuir–Blodgett (LB) method to investigate the effects of structural orientation on their electrical and reservoir computing properties. Polarized ultraviolet–visible absorption spectroscopy and atomic force microscopy revealed that repeated compression–expansion cycles during LB deposition produced highly oriented SWCNT nanofilms. The oriented films exhibited an anisotropic electrical response, pronounced hysteretic current–voltage characteristics, and enhanced generation of higher-order harmonics, while water adsorption further enhanced the current and nonlinear electrical response. In waveform generation tasks, the advantage of the highly oriented films was most pronounced for the sawtooth and sin(2ω) targets, which involve more complex waveform features and frequency components. Additional delayed-input reconstruction and nonlinear autoregressive moving average (NARMA) 2 tasks revealed enhanced fading memory and nonlinear temporal processing under humidified conditions, with the highly oriented film exhibiting a larger memory capacity and lower NARMA2 error than the less-oriented film. These results indicate that structural orientation, together with humidity-dependent electrical dynamics, contributes to the nonlinear and temporal information-processing capabilities of SWCNT–PmPV nanofilms. These findings provide a practical strategy for modulating in-material reservoir computing performance through structural control of anisotropic material networks.

title: Coupled Regulation of Oxygen-Vacancy-Modified Near-Surface Structure and Interfacial Stability for High-Performance Li-Rich Mn-Based Cathodes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Li-rich Mn-based layered oxides (LRMOs) are prospective next-generation cathodes, delivering high specific capacities via coupled cationic and anionic redox. However, sluggish reaction kinetics, irreversible oxygen loss, and progressive interfacial structural degradation limit the practical application of LRMOs. Herein, a coupled strategy for regulating the near-surface structure and interfacial stability is developed using ammonium titanyl oxalate (ATO) as a multifunctional precursor. During thermal treatment, an approximately 10 nm Li2TiO3 coating layer forms to stabilize the cathode interface. Meanwhile, reducing gases released from precursor decomposition induce oxygen vacancy formation, whereas Ti incorporation suppresses excessive transition-metal (TM) reduction in the near-surface region, thereby alleviating the associated increase in Mn3+ content and Jahn–Teller distortion. Moreover, the coupled Ti and oxygen vacancy configuration enhances anionic redox reversibility, stabilizes the near-surface oxygen framework, and lowers the Li+ migration barrier, thereby improving Li+ transport and structural stability. The optimized ATO-2% cathode achieves an average initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 90.07% at 0.1 C and a capacity retention of 88.1% after 300 cycles at 1 C. This work establishes a coupled regulation strategy for the oxygen vacancy-modified near-surface structure and interfacial stability, providing a route for optimizing oxygen vacancy engineering in LRMO cathodes.

title: Diverse Impact of Ionic Liquid Additives on Lubricant Electrical Conductivity
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The electrical conductivity (EC) of the lubricating oils and greases in electric vehicles should be neither too high nor too low. Primarily, these lubricants serve as electrical insulators with high dielectric strength to prevent current leakage or short circuits. On the other hand, lubricants with extremely low conductivity can lead to buildup of electrostatic charges at the tribological interfaces, potentially resulting in arcing and associated surface pitting. Ionic liquids (ILs) have recently been developed as candidate lubricant additives. ILs are ionic in nature and thus are intuitively expected to increase the lubricant EC. However, there is a lack of a quantitative measure of the exact impact and fundamental understanding of the correlation with IL chemistry. In this work, we measured the change in oil EC upon introducing several oil-miscible ILs as additives at various concentrations and temperatures and modeled the relationship using the Arrhenius equation. Most ILs substantially increased the oil EC as expected. For example, adding 1 wt % of aprotic phosphate ILs, such as [N8888][DEHP] and [P8888][DEHP], to PAO4 boosted the EC by two to three orders of magnitude. In contrast, adding 1 wt % of other types of ILs, such as [N888H][DEHP], [P66614][C7H15COO], [P66614][C17H35COO], and [P66614][BTMPP], increased the oil EC by one to two orders of magnitude. A protic IL has less effect on the oil EC than an aprotic IL likely due to its hydrogen-bonding interactions between the cations and anions leading to reduced charge carrier mobility. Furthermore, the protic IL [N888H][DEHP] was surprisingly found to decrease the oil EC when added into a fully formulated lubricant, possibly due to competitive interactions with certain additives in the package that hinder the mobility of charge carriers. Overall, these results provide fundamental insight into the impact of IL molecular structures on oil EC and offer guidance for future development of ILs for advanced lubrication.

title: Combustion of Boron Nanoparticles Encapsulated within Perchlorate Matrices: A Mechanistic Study
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Boron is an attractive high-energy fuel, but its practical combustion efficiency is limited by a viscous oxide layer that impedes oxygen transport and promotes agglomeration. Here, we address these limitations by assembling boron nanoparticles into spray-dried mesoparticles in which boron is encapsulated within an ammonium perchlorate (AP) matrix and a nitrocellulose binder. This architecture enhances fuel oxidizer proximity, accelerates AP decomposition onset by ∼60 °C, and enhances reaction kinetics as evidenced by a ∼50% pressurization rate and a ∼58% shorter burn time relative to the physically mixed formulation. In situ TEM, TGA/DSC, and T-jump time-of-flight mass spectrometry reveal that mesoparticles promote interfacial reactions producing both B2O3 and boron nitride (BN). BN formation is identified as a thermodynamic efficiency-loss pathway, releasing significantly less energy per mole of boron than oxidation to B2O3. Substituting AP with potassium perchlorate eliminates the nitrogen source, significantly reducing BN formation, and further improves combustion performance. These results demonstrate that mesoscale encapsulation combined with targeted oxidizer selection provides a practical strategy to enhance boron combustion efficiency.

title: Dimensionality and Nanoporosity Effects on the Electrochemical Reactivity of Ti-Oxo Metal–Organic Frameworks
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) incorporating redox-active metal–oxo clusters offer an emerging platform for diverse applications, including electrochemical energy storage, yet their electrochemical reactivity remains largely unexplored. Here, we report the first systematic electrochemical investigation of Ti-MOFs in aqueous electrolytes, focusing on the microporous Ti tetracarboxylate MIP-177 family, which exists in two polymorphs featuring either discrete Ti12O15 oxoclusters (MIP-177-LT) or infinite one-dimensional Ti-oxo nanowires (MIP-177-HT). Using cyclic voltammetry and galvanostatic cycling, we demonstrate that only MIP-177-HT exhibits measurable electronic conductivity, enabled by its extended 1D metal–oxo network, whereas MIP-177-LT remains electronically insulating. Deconvolution of Faradaic and non-Faradaic contributions across different aqueous electrolytes indicates that the internal nanoporosity of MIP-177-HT significantly enhances double-layer charge storage. In LiCl electrolytes, MIP-177-HT also undergoes reversible Li+ insertion with thermodynamic behavior comparable to anatase TiO2, but with markedly reduced voltage hysteresis. Galvanostatic cycling in this electrolyte delivers a capacity of 60 mAh g–1 with a Coulombic efficiency of 97% at 0.11 A g–1, demonstrating the almost absence of parasitic hydrogen evolution. Nonetheless, post-cycling X-ray diffraction analyses reveal pronounced structural degradation of MIP-177-HT, indicating insufficient stability for long-term aqueous operation. Overall, these findings establish the fundamental electrochemical behavior of Ti-oxo MOFs and underscore the need to enhance their structural robustness to fully exploit their potential in aqueous-based energy storage applications.

title: Nanoscale Interfacial Engineering of Printable Polysaccharide Hydrogels for Simultaneous High Porosity and Wet-State Mechanical Robustness
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Direct ink writing (DIW) provides a promising route to fabricate porous hydrogel constructs with programmable architectures, yet highly hydrated printed networks often suffer from swelling-induced softening and structural instability under wet conditions. Herein, we report a nanoscale interfacial engineering strategy for DIW of mechanically robust, hierarchically porous polysaccharide hydrogels. Purified silanol-rich silica-fume nanoparticles were incorporated into a sodium alginate/chitosan polyelectrolyte ink, followed by printing, freeze-drying, and sequential acetic acid/Ca2+ crosslinking. The resulting SCS hydrogels showed well-preserved printed architectures, interconnected pore networks, and homogeneous silica distribution. Silica–polysaccharide hydrogen-bonding interfaces, SA/CS polyelectrolyte complexation, and Ca2+-mediated alginate crosslinking jointly formed a constrained multilevel network that suppressed swelling-induced structural loosening. Consequently, the SCS hydrogels maintained porosity above 90%, reduced equilibrium swelling by approximately 70% compared with the single-network control, and achieved a wet-state compressive modulus of 913 kPa through combined nanoscale interfacial reinforcement and programmable printed architecture, while exhibiting good structural recovery under cyclic deformation. In vitro evaluations further indicated favorable cytocompatibility and osteogenesis-related cellular responses, supporting further evaluation of SCS hydrogels as mechanically stable printable bio-based scaffolds for bone-tissue-engineering-related applications. This work demonstrates a DIW-compatible nanoscale interfacial design strategy for decoupling high porosity from swelling-induced softening and wet-state mechanical deterioration, providing a useful structure–property-processing design framework for structurally stable porous hydrogel materials.

title: Voltage-Driven Transition from Steady-State Fluctuations to Phase-Transition Noise in Nanoscale VO2 Devices
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract We investigate the electrically driven metal-to-insulator transition (MIT) in a nanoscale vanadium dioxide (VO2) Mott memristor through noise spectroscopy and two-dimensional resistor network simulations. Our experiments focus on both the insulating phase as the applied voltage approaches the threshold voltage (set transition) and the metallic phase as the voltage is reduced toward the reset voltage (reset transition). In both regimes, we observe an order-of-magnitude increase in relative current noise near the transition points. To analyze the origin of this noise enhancement, we use simulations that capture the stochastic dynamics of the phase transition. The simulations indicate that the increased noise stems from amplified phase fluctuations near the switching threshold, where competing metallic and insulating domains lead to the dynamic reconfiguration of conduction paths. In addition, we show that the precursor current fluctuations observed near the switching threshold have a relative magnitude comparable to the cycle-to-cycle threshold voltage variation, indicating that transition-related fluctuations may remain a limiting factor for the achievable threshold voltage variation in optimized devices. These findings provide a comprehensive picture of the noise performance of VO2 devices, capturing the heavily voltage-dependent noise characteristics all along the switching cycle.

title: Silk Fibroin Nanoparticles Coated with an Extracellular Vesicle–Liposome Hybrid Shell for Controlled Cargo Delivery
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Silk fibroin nanoparticles (SFNPs) are promising nanocarriers for drug delivery owing to their biocompatibility, bioactivity, controllable biodegradability, and low toxicity. However, their translation is limited by formulation-dependent variations in morphology, colloidal stability, drug loading, and aggregation, all of which can affect release behavior and biological performance. Here, we investigated how fibroin solubilization conditions govern the self-assembly, internal structure, surface properties, and cargo delivery performance of SFNPs, using curcumin as a hydrophobic model compound. SFNPs were prepared by lithium bromide (LiBr) solubilization followed by desolvation and were characterized using complementary scattering, microscopy, and spectroscopy techniques. Fibroin solubilization temperature and curcumin loading modulated SFNP size, internal organization, and surface roughness. In particular, SFNPs formed 70–150 nm mass-fractal aggregates composed of smaller primary nanoparticles, and this morphology affected cargo loading and release by controlling accessible internal surface area and solvent contact. To further stabilize the system and engineer the external interface, SFNPs were incorporated into a liposome/extracellular vesicle (EV) hybrid shell by sonication, generating a carrier-in-carrier system containing EV-derived membrane-associated components. The hybrid lipid–EV/SFNP platform reduced aggregation in aqueous media and provided a tunable external shell for controlled release of hydrophobic cargo. Overall, this work establishes a structure-based proof of concept connecting upstream solubilization parameters to downstream nanoparticle architecture, supporting the rational design of hybrid silk-based nanocarriers for cargo delivery.

title: Three-Dimensional Folded Electrode Smart Finger Sleeve Based on a Silica Reinforced Ionic Hydrogel Composite for Multidirectional Tactile Sensing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Human fingers can perceive multidirectional tactile information through spatially distributed mechanoreceptors, thereby enabling delicate manipulation and interactive behaviors. However, most existing wearable tactile sensors primarily focus on unidirectional normal force detection, making it difficult to effectively recognize direction-related tactile inputs. Here, we report a three-dimensional finger sleeve that spatially encodes multidirectional mechanical stimuli into distinguishable multichannel piezoresistive signals by integrating spatially distributed folded electrodes and an ionic hydrogel sensing layer within a three-dimensional TPU supporting structure. The localized thin-walled groove design enhanced deformation concentration and force transmission, while the incorporation of 1 wt % SiO2 improved the hydrogel sensitivity by approximately 77%. The SiO2 nanoparticles were proposed to serve as dispersed rigid nodes, amplifying local strain gradients and deformation-induced changes in ion migration pathways. The device exhibited stable piezoresistive responses under normal forces of 0–20 N, enabled directional discrimination under shear forces of 0–5 N, and further detected an out-of-plane torque of 3 × 10–4 N·m together with its directional information. The distinguishable multichannel tactile patterns further enabled accurate gesture recognition and a two-dimensional direction-digit authentication strategy, in which directional information was introduced as an additional input dimension to enhance password complexity. This work provides a versatile strategy for wearable multidirectional tactile perception and offers possibilities for secure human–machine interaction, wearable control, and intelligent robotic sensing.

title: A Robust Bifunctional Envelope for Synergistic Superhydrophobic Anti-Icing and Electrothermal Deicing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Integrating passive superhydrophobic anti-icing with active electrothermal deicing offers a promising approach to ice protection. However, conventional layered designs often suffer from weak interfacial adhesion and limited heat transfer between the superhydrophobic layer and the underlying heater. Here, we develop a robust superhydrophobic anti-icing and electrothermal deicing bifunctional envelope by incorporating nanoporous polydivinylbenzene into a nickel-foam framework. The resulting monolithic composite combines mechanical durability, whole-body superhydrophobicity and electrothermal heating. Its capabilities are evidenced by retained superhydrophobicity after 3000 friction cycles, prolonged icing time, a low ice adhesion strength of 3.3 kPa, and efficient electrothermal deicing. Direct laser writing tailors the conductive network, reducing deicing energy consumption by 76.8% relative to the unpatterned composite and enabling thick ice to melt within 24 s at a low power density of 0.43 W/cm2. The flexibility and patternability of the envelope allow conformal integration onto curved surfaces, providing a route to durable surfaces that combine passive anti-icing with active deicing.

title: Binary-Crosslinked Alginate/Zwitterionic Interpenetrating Polymer Network Coatings for Lubricious and Antifouling Urinary Catheters
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Hydrophilic hydrogel coatings can mitigate catheter-associated infections and friction-induced mucosal trauma during urinary catheterization by providing hydration-driven lubrication and antifouling surfaces. Here, we report an alginate/sulfobetaine methacrylate-based zwitterionic interpenetrating polymer network (Alg-ZW IPN) that integrates a binary crosslinker system into the IPN architecture by pairing a short-chain crosslinker, N,N′-methylenebisacrylamide (MbAm), with a long-chain crosslinker, poly(ethylene glycol) dimethacrylate (PEGDMA). In the binary crosslinked IPN (Alg-ZW BIPN), MbAm establishes dense local junctions for structural integrity, while PEGDMA spans the interjunction domains to mechanically bridge the network, confine alginate chains, and stabilize Ca2+–alginate coordination. This architecture redistributes mechanical stress across length scales, thereby improving coating durability. The Alg-ZW BIPN coating exhibited ultralow friction, with a friction coefficient of 0.01–0.02, and maintained 49% lower friction than MbAm single crosslinker coatings. In catheter insertion tests using a standard vascular phantom, the coating reduced insertion force by up to 75% compared with uncoated catheters. The coating also inhibited Escherichia coli adhesion by 97.4% relative to uncoated substrates and showed excellent biocompatibility, with a hemolysis ratio of 0.17% and >95% endothelial cell viability after 24 h. Overall, the Alg-ZW BIPN design provides a general and scalable route to mechanically robust, lubricious, and antifouling hydrogel interfaces for indwelling medical devices.

title: Tuning Inter- and Intraparticle Crosslinking and Packing Density Governs the 3D Bioprintability and Biological Performance
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Granular hydrogels are an emerging class of microporous biomaterials assembled from annealable microparticles that enhance cell survival, function, infiltration, and cell migration through their interconnected cell-scale void spaces. Here, we aimed to understand how balancing inter- and intraparticle interactions, alongside microparticle packing density, influences the printability and cellular responses of granular hydrogels. Mechanically fragmented microparticles, made of tyramine-modified alginate (TAlg) and gelatin (TGel), underwent primary enzymatic gelation and secondary photocrosslinking for construct stabilization. Balancing this two-scale chemical trade-off yielded a compressive modulus of 12.9–24.7 kPa, while rapid photoinitiator clearance (>90% within 1 h) ensured high cytocompatibility. Incorporating 10–40 vol % interstitial matrix tuned total porosity from ∼7 to 18%, with medium-packed inks (20 vol % matrix) achieving high fidelity for three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting without sacrificing void connectivity. The resulting interconnected network accelerated cell infiltration to a depth of 450 μm within 3 days (∼3-fold higher than bulk hydrogels) and enabled ex vivo tissue adhesion (7.1 kPa shear strength). 3D-bioprinted granular constructs supported dense interconnected 3D cellular network formation over 7 days. This scalable strategy to deconstruct di-tyramine-mediated bulk hydrogels provides a versatile toolbox for advanced biofabrication and complex tissue engineering.

title: Chloroacetate Buffer-Modified SnO2 Electron Transport Layer for Efficient Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Tin oxide (SnO2) is a popular material for the electron transport layer (ETL) in perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, the defects at the SnO2/perovskite interface tend to induce non-radiative recombination and deprotonation of formamidinium (FA+), limiting the device performance. Herein, a chloroacetate (CA) buffer system consisting of chloroacetic acid and its potassium salt was employed as a unique multifunctional interface modifier to synergistically engineer the SnO2 ETL/perovskite interface. The chloroacetate anion anchors to Sn and Pb sites, while the chloroacetic acid stabilizes FA+ through the hydrogen bond. As a result, the acidic buffer system suppresses FA+ deprotonation, enhances perovskite film quality, and improves carrier transport. Consequently, the CA buffer-modified PSC devices achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 24.8%, considerably higher than 22.6% for the control devices. They also demonstrate prolonged dark-storage stability; particularly, the unencapsulated devices retain 99% of initial efficiency after 1500 h of ambient storage. This work shows that combining an organic acid and its conjugated base offers a facile yet effective strategy to simultaneously passivate the buried interface and stabilize perovskite components for efficient and stable PSCs.

title: Synergistic Molecular-Nano Engineering Enabling Ultralong-Cycling and High-Capacity Lithium Storage of Covalent Organic Frameworks
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lithium-ion capacitors (LICs) combine the high energy density of batteries with the high-power density of supercapacitors for potential advanced applications. As promising anode candidates for LICs, the practical application of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) is hampered by the intrinsically low electronic conductivity. Here, a “molecular-nano” dual-scale synergistic strategy is proposed to enhance the charge transport and utilization of active sites. At the molecular scale, three highly crystalized COFs (2,6-DAAQ-COF, 2,6-DAA-COF, and 1,4-DAAQ-COF) via donor-acceptor (D–A) structural design are synthesized to enhance the intramolecular charge separation and electron transfer processes. At the nanoscale, a three-dimensional conductive network is constructed by in situ compositing with carbon nanotubes (CNTs) to yield core-shell structured COF@CNT, which also effectively exfoliates COF layers and exposes active sites. Benefiting from the synergistic enhancement between intramolecular charge transfer and the macroscopic conductive network, the optimized 2,6-DAAQ-COF@CNT50 exhibits exceptional lithium storage performance, retaining a high discharge capacity of 1983 mAh g–1 after 1000 cycles at 1 A g–1. Furthermore, the electrode also exhibits excellent electrochemical performance at low temperature (–20 °C), retaining 220 mAh g–1 after 2000 cycles at 0.5 A g–1. The assembled LICs demonstrate superior stability of up to 10,000 cycles. This study provides a new strategy and mechanistic insights for designing high-performance organic anode materials for LICs.

title: Recent Progress in the Reutilization of Epoxy Resins: Strategies after End-of-Life
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The production and demand for thermosetting epoxy resins have been increasing steadily, and the massive decommissioning of equipment has generated a substantial volume of solid waste that urgently requires proper disposal. The stable three-dimensional crosslinked networks of epoxy resins endow them with excellent service performance, yet simultaneously render them difficult to recycle after retirement. The accumulation of such waste not only leads to resource wastage but also exacerbates environmental pollution. Meanwhile, growing concerns over fossil resource depletion have reinforced the strategic importance of recognizing end-of-life materials as a renewable resource. This review focuses on current strategies for the reutilization of waste epoxy resins. Based on the end-application of the regenerated products, the strategies fall into three categories: (i) polymeric derivatives, including both remanufactured epoxy materials and non-epoxy polymers; (ii) functional material applications; and (iii) small-molecule products. For each pathway, the chemical rationale and major challenges are discussed. This review aims to provide a framework for understanding current utilization approaches for waste epoxy resin, facilitating the transition of thermosetting waste from a disposal burden to a valuable resource base.

title: Bromide-Rich Phase Enhances the Photovoltaic Performance in Fabricating the Hybrid Wide-Bandgap Perovskite-Based Solar Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Nowadays, high-performance tandem solar cells may be fabricated by connecting the organic–inorganic hybrid wide-bandgap (WBG) halide perovskite film-based solar cells (PSCs) with the silicon-based one. The major challenge for both academia and industry is the performance of the WBG-based solar cell. Here, to improve the efficiency and stability of WBG PSCs, ethylenediammonium halides are designed to passivate and exclude the defects in fabricating the WBG-based solar cells. Ethylenediammonium bromide forms a Br-rich phase, which not only passivates surface defects but also suppresses light-induced phase segregation, thereby improving the performance of WBG mixed-halide PSCs. The champion PSCs achieve an open-circuit voltage of 1.255 V, a fill factor of 84.12%, and a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 23.64%. Device stability is also markedly enhanced, with 99.6% of the initial PCE retained after 1728 h under ISOS-D-1I conditions and a T80 lifetime of 1020 h under ISOS-T-1I conditions. This work provides a new insight into optimization strategies for mixed-halide WBG perovskites.

title: Is the sixth great extinction imminent? Scientists must draw on natural history for clues
abstract: A lack of crosstalk between research disciplines is hampering scholars’ ability to fully examine how people have altered Earth’s biodiversity.

title: Suppressing Photoinduced Phase Segregation in Wide-Bandgap Perovskites via Guanidinium-Thiocyanate-Mediated Electrical Homogenization
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Wide-bandgap perovskites are pivotal for tandem photovoltaics but suffer from photoinduced halide segregation, where grain boundaries (GBs) act as hotspots for ion redistribution. Here, we show that suppressing this instability is associated with coordinated grain-growth regulation and more uniform electrical response across grain interiors and grain boundaries. Among the four thiocyanate (SCN–)-based additives, GASCN produces a compact, predominantly large-grained morphology accompanied by more uniform nanoscale current distribution. Correlative photoluminescence (PL) and time-resolved PL mapping further indicate that GASCN treatment suppresses photoinduced carrier accumulation at GBs, a phenomenon pronounced in small-grained regions. Kelvin probe force microscopy further uncovers that GASCN induces an inversion of the GB surface potential, reconstructing the local electrostatic environment to oppose halide redistribution under illumination. As a result, GASCN-treated films exhibit stabilized absorption edges, negligible PL peak shifts, and suppressed lattice expansion upon light soaking. Combined with interfacial passivation, the devices deliver a champion power conversion efficiency of 20.25% with an open-circuit voltage of 1.34 V. This work establishes coordinated grain-growth regulation and nanoscale electrical homogenization as a design principle for stabilizing mixed-halide perovskites, and provides direct nanoscale evidence for electrostatic modulation at GBs as a suppression mechanism against photoinduced phase segregation.

title: Scale-Dependent Friction in Rough SiO2/Single-Crystal MoS2 Contacts
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The scale limits of superlubricity in realistic multiasperity contacts remain poorly understood. Although lateral atomic-force cancellation in incommensurate or disordered interfaces can generate low friction, how experimentally accessible contact size, local stress state, and load distribution regulate this scale-dependent behavior remains unclear. Here, we investigate the scale-dependent shear strength of SiO2 glass sphere/single-crystal MoS2 contacts with different sphere radii using atomic force microscopy and a custom microtribometer across extended load ranges. By combining power spectral density-based random rough surface generation with boundary element method simulations, we evaluate a dimensionless contact-scale parameter ai/bcore,i defined by the ratio between contact-patch radius and a characteristic elastic core width in rough multiasperity interfaces. The results show that the effective shear strength decreases continuously with increasing real contact area at small-to-intermediate contact scales, consistent with enhanced statistical cancellation of lateral atomic forces expected for disordered interfaces. As contact scale further increases, this reduction is progressively suppressed as the maximum scale parameter (ai/bcore,i)max approaches unity and an increasing fraction of the load is carried by contact patches satisfying ai/bcore,i > 1. The R = 2.5 mm probe condition exhibits a higher effective shear strength and a broader simulated contact-pressure distribution than the smaller-probe conditions. However, because sphere radius and the measured roughness spectrum were not independently varied, these differences cannot be attributed uniquely to sphere curvature. Instead, they reflect the combined influence of probe geometry, roughness statistics, and the resulting multiasperity contact state. Our results establish a multiscale framework linking atomic-force cancellation, finite contact-size effects, and rough-contact statistics, revealing how structural superlubricity gradually loses its scale invariance in realistic multiasperity interfaces.

title: Promoting CO 2 Electromethanation via Reverse H‐Spillover on Zeolite Y‐Confined CuO Nanoclusters
abstract: ABSTRACT The electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction reaction (eCO 2 RR) presents a promising route for converting CO 2 emissions into valuable products, with methane (CH 4 ) being particularly attractive owing to its high energy density and infrastructure compatibility. However, selective CH 4 formation via sequential *CO hydrogenation remains kinetically challenged by competing C–C coupling pathways. Here, we encapsulate CuO nanoclusters within zeolite Y, where spatial confinement enables the uniform dispersion of CuO and enhances the reverse H‐spillover (RHS)‐mediated utilization of *H species generated on the zeolite support for sequential *CO hydrogenation. The optimized catalyst achieves a CH 4 Faradaic efficiency of 71.7% ± 1.3% at 600 mA cm −2 and 65.6% ± 1.0% at 1000 mA cm −2 . Experimental and theoretical studies show that H 2 O is preferentially activated on the zeolite support, generating *H species that are rapidly transferred to adjacent CuO via RHS for CO 2 hydrogenation. Operando spectroscopic detection of CH 4 ‐related *OCH 3 /*CH x intermediates, together with DFT calculations, indicates that zeolite–CuO interactions favor *CO hydrogenation to *CHO over *CO dimerization, thereby promoting CH 4 formation. This work establishes spatial confinement‐coupled RHS as an effective strategy for regulating interfacial *H transfer and sequential hydrogenation in the eCO 2 RR process.

title: Rationale‐Guided and Iterative Learning for Redesigning a Highly Enantio‐ and Chemoselective Flavin‐Dependent Phenolic Hydroxylase
abstract: ABSTRACT Flavin‐dependent monooxygenases (FDMOs) can catalyze C─H hydroxylation of phenolic compounds, yet the scope of their application has never been challenged beyond the hydroxylation of simple substrates nor explored for the ability to achieve selective hydroxylation. FDMO hydroxylation is often poorly controlled, yielding unstable, multiply hydroxylated products. Here, we used a mechanistic insight‐guided iterative learning workflow to redesign the active site of p ‐hydroxyphenylacetate hydroxylase to expand its capability for chemo‐ and enantioselective control in the synthesis of ( R )‐norepinephrine. Within only three rounds of an engineering campaign, a DISD_LG variant that switched from ( S )‐ to ( R )‐selective hydroxylation was obtained with excellent enantioselectivity (97.6%ee ( R )). This variant also produced markedly fewer multiply hydroxylated products (R )‐norepinephrine was obtained with 48.8% isolated yield and 96.2%ee ( R ). The molecular mechanisms underlying the enantio‐ and chemoselective control achieved by the DISD_LG variant were elucidated using molecular dynamics simulations. This work presents an enzyme engineering workflow to achieve kinetic resolution in combination with a controllable degree of hydroxylation, the aspects previously overlooked or underemphasized in FDMOs.

title: Exciton-phonon interaction suppression enables efficient near-infrared perovskite quantum dot LEDs
abstract: In energy-transfer light emitters, lattice vibrations can drain energy before recombination and reduce near-infrared emission efficiency. This study uses an ion-pair treatment to change the surface of Yb-doped perovskite quantum dots, which reduces vibration-related losses and improves energy transfer. The resulting devices produce efficient, bright near-infrared light under electrical operation. The findings suggest that controlling lattice dynamics through surface chemistry can improve this dual-channel emitter.

title: From biological principles to battery interfaces: recent progress in bio-inspired design for aqueous zinc-ion batteries
Robotic inspection and maintenance for energy infrastructure: a systematic review and future perspectives
Data center cooling in the AI era: cross-scale challenges and system-level outlook
abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) is fundamentally reshaping data center thermal and energy requirements, driven by increasing power densities and heterogeneous workload characteristics. This review provides an integrated cross-scale and temporal perspective that connects AI heat generation with chip-, rack-, and facility-scale thermal management and their interactions with external energy, water, and grid infrastructures. Modern AI workloads, enabled by accelerator-based hardware, can generate highly localized and temporally dynamic heat fluxes, challenging traditional assumptions of uniform and steady-state cooling design. Accordingly, a range of cooling technologies is examined, including air-based systems, liquid cooling approaches, hybrid configurations, and heat-reuse strategies, with emphasis on their performance limits and deployment constraints. The analysis further identifies key cross-cutting barriers to scalability and efficiency, including thermodynamic irreversibility, coupled water–energy–grid dependencies, cross-scale thermal interactions, reliability and maintainability constraints, and technology-specific trade-offs. Building on these observations, future cooling systems are expected to shift toward integrated and adaptive designs that prioritize multi-objective optimization rather than isolated performance improvements. Emerging directions include grid-responsive and water-aware operation, thermal storage-enabled temporal decoupling, co-designed computing and cooling infrastructures, and predictive closed-loop thermal management enabled by digital twins and data-driven control. Collectively, the findings highlight a transition from component-level optimization toward fully integrated system architectures that jointly optimize energy efficiency, resource utilization, operational resilience, and computational performance across spatial and temporal scales.

title: Advances in sorption-based thermochemical energy storage: from material properties to prototype-level performance
Common-path evaluation of electric boiler and thermal storage dispatch in Finnish district heating under electricity-price uncertainty
abstract: The value of uncertainty-aware district-heating dispatch depends on when prices become known and how long heat remains in storage. This study develops a price-taking mixed-integer linear model for a Finnish system with biomass CHP, a 50 MW th electric boiler (EB), a natural-gas peak boiler, and thermal energy storage (TES). Daily 72 h problems implement the cleared first 24 h and propagate each policy's realised TES state. Deterministic, stochastic, and budgeted robust policies are compared on one 2023 hourly path and on 800 held-out price trajectories; their economic differences are assessed against TES value and parameter sensitivity. With 200 MWh th TES, annual costs are EUR 4.902, 4.920, and 4.939 million, respectively, compared with EUR 4.783 million for a rolling perfect-foresight benchmark. Stochastic dispatch has the lowest held-out mean cost and regret, while deterministic dispatch has slightly lower P 95 and CVaR 95 . TES saves EUR 1.974 million a − 1 relative to matched no-storage dispatch; the stochastic and robust annual premiums are only EUR 0.037 and 0.075/MWh th . Storage mainly shifts heat within one day. A 200-sample annual rolling sensitivity analysis identifies CHP power-to-heat ratio, EB capacity, fuel price, and TES duration as the dominant cost drivers. Biases of ±5% and ± 10% in look-ahead heat demand preserve the annual policy ranking. The EB dispatch-weighted carbon intensity is approximately 26 g CO2/kWhel, below the national consumption-weighted mean of 37.69 g CO2/kWhel.

title: Pronounced Visible‐Light Cryptochirality Detection of Various Terpenoids via Helical Polyaromatic Capsules
abstract: ABSTRACT Cryptochirality refers to molecular chirality with undetectable/absent circular dichroism (CD) bands. Whereas there have been several host compounds capable of binding cryptochiral biosubstrates for their analysis, those with guest‐induced CD activity in the visible region remain quite rare so far. We herein report the host‐guest interaction‐based CD analysis of various terpenoids using two different, helical polyaromatic capsules under ambient aqueous conditions. When one molecule of CD‐inactive monoterpenoid, (–)‐carvone, is quantitatively encapsulated within a CD‐inactive capsule bearing a spheroidal cavity, the resultant host‐guest complex displays pronounced CD bands in the range of 350–430 nm with a relatively high absolute molar circular dichroism value (i.e., |Δ ε | >80 M −1 cm −1 at ∼390 nm), derived from the guest‐induced host helicity. The chirality of other cryptochiral mono/sesquiterpenoids is also detected with similar efficiency (∼30–90 M −1 cm −1 ). The enantiomeric excess (%ee) of d/l ‐mixtures of monoterpenoids can be determined with the helical cavity via comparative CD analysis. By the use of another larger capsule, di‐ and triterpenoids also induce its intense CD bands (up to ∼130 M −1 cm −1 ) in the visible region upon encapsulation. The present study highlights the potential application of helical polyaromatic hosts to the facile cryptochiral analysis of a broad range of biosubstrates with intense CD output.

title: One Acceptor Core, Two Bright Pathways: CF 3 ‐Substituted Triazines Achieve Highly Efficient Intermolecular Exciplexes and Intramolecular TADF
abstract: ABSTRACT Intermolecular charge‐transfer (CT)‐based exciplexes provide broad design flexibility through independent donor and acceptor selection, but often suffer from low photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) due to limited orbital overlap. In contrast, intramolecular CT‐based thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) systems can achieve high PLQYs through controlled donor‐acceptor interactions, but generally require precise molecular design and substituent tuning. Here, we show that a CF 3 ‐substituted triazine scaffold ( T4 ) serves as a unified molecular platform for achieving highly efficient emission through both intermolecular and intramolecular CT pathways. The CzCF 3 ‐substituted derivatives T4‐2CzCF 3 and T4‐3CzCF 3 formed highly emissive intermolecular exciplexes with mCBP, achieving PLQYs of 100%. Incorporation of stronger carbazole donors afforded T4‐3Cz , which exhibited intramolecular CT‐based TADF with PLQYs reaching 100% in solution and 100% in an mCBP‐doped film. T4‐3Cz also displayed near‐infrared multiphoton absorption, with a two‐photon absorption cross‐section (σ 2 ) of 80 GM at 780 nm and a three‐photon absorption cross‐section (σ 3 ) of 2.94 × 10 −80 cm 6 s 2 at 1210 nm. Furthermore, OLEDs based on the T4‐3CzCF 3 intermolecular exciplex and the intramolecular CT‐based TADF emitter T4‐3Cz exhibited efficient electroluminescent performance. These findings establish the T4 scaffold as a versatile molecular framework that integrates highly efficient intermolecular exciplex TADF, intramolecular CT‐based TADF, multiphoton absorption, and OLED functionality.

title: Stimulus-Driven Reconfigurable Memristors with Volatile-to-Nonvolatile Transition for Spatiotemporal Neuromorphic Computing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Neuromorphic hardware for spatiotemporal information processing requires both transient dynamics and programmable weight storage, whereas existing implementations typically rely either on heterogeneous integration of volatile dynamic units and nonvolatile memory devices or on compliance-current regulation to reconfigure volatile/nonvolatile operation within a single device, increasing device diversity or peripheral control complexity. This work reports a stimulus-reconfigurable Ag/ZnS/FTO memristor in which the stability of Ag conductive pathways is regulated by the strength and temporal scale of external stimuli, enabling volatile short-term dynamics and nonvolatile conductance modulation within a single device. Under weak or short stimuli, the device exhibits multiscale short-term plasticity governed by pulse amplitude, width, interval, and number, enabling Morse-code temporal encoding. Under strong or prolonged stimuli, it realizes long-term potentiation/depression and multilevel conductance modulation. Leveraging this dual-mode behavior, a volatile–nonvolatile reservoir computing architecture is constructed, where volatile responses act as reservoir states for dynamic feature expansion and nonvolatile conductance stores readout weights. For spatial image recognition, the architecture achieves 92.94 and 82.27% accuracies on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST, respectively, with an estimated 84.5% fewer devices than a purely nonvolatile multilayer perceptron. The same architecture further achieves 96.13% accuracy and a 95.14% Macro F1 score in ECG heartbeat classification, highlighting a unified device strategy for hardware-efficient spatiotemporal neuromorphic computing.

title: Exchange-Bias-Gated Temporal Memory in PtMn/NiFe Heterostructures for Physical Pattern Recognition
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Physical information processing relies on the ability of a dynamical system to transform external stimuli into distinguishable internal states. Although nonlinear magnetization dynamics in magnetic materials exhibit memory and rich dynamical behavior, engineering responses that depend on the temporal ordering of inputs remains a central challenge for spintronics-based physical computing. Here, we show that exchange-biased PtMn/NiFe heterostructures create input-selective magnetic state spaces through history-dependent magnetization dynamics driven by microwave excitation. Above a threshold microwave power, nonlinear excitation modifies the interfacial magnetic configuration so that sequences delivering identical total excitation energy but differing in temporal order evolve into distinct resonance states. Short four-bit microwave pulse sequences generate sixteen experimentally distinguishable magnetic resonance conditions, with only a selective subset of patterns producing large state transitions and yielding sparse activation. Using the shifted resonance fields as physical features, a multinomial logistic regression classifier achieves 88.5% accuracy on the Modified National Institute of Standards and Technology (MNIST) handwritten-digit recognition task. These results establish exchange-biased antiferromagnet/ferromagnet interfaces as an effective platform for engineering history-dependent magnetic state spaces and demonstrate that the interfacial spin dynamics can perform temporal information processing of short pulse sequences directly in hardware, with relevance to edge artificial intelligence, radar, and sensing applications.

title: Hydroxy-Functionalized n-Type OMIECs as Multifunctional Conductive Biointerfaces for Simplified Biosensor Fabrication
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors (OMIECs) have emerged as key materials for bioelectronics owing to their ability to couple ionic and electronic transport. However, their potential as multifunctional biointerfaces for biosensing remains largely untapped, particularly for n-type systems. Here, we report a hydroxy-functionalized n-doped poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO-OH) that unifies efficient electron transport and enzyme immobilization within a single material platform. By introducing terminal hydroxy groups into the polymer backbone, PBFDO-OH enables the direct immobilization of glucose dehydrogenase through a simple one-pot strategy, eliminating the gold substrates, self-assembled monolayers, and multistep surface activation protocols that underpin conventional biosensor fabrication. This streamlined approach yields robust biofunctional electrodes with enhanced electrochemical performance while preserving enzyme activity and long-term stability. Integrated with additively manufactured electrodes, the resulting glucose biosensor demonstrates a high sensitivity of 17.4 μA L mmol–1, a low detection limit of 3.42 μmol L-1, excellent reproducibility (RSD = 5.35%), reliable quantification in human serum (RSD

title: HIFU-Enhanced Transdermal Delivery of Hyaluronic-Acid-Functionalized Solid Lipid Nanoparticles for Localized Melanoma Therapy
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Cutaneous melanoma is an aggressive skin cancer for which localized treatment remains difficult because of limited drug penetration through the stratum corneum and the systemic toxicity of conventional chemotherapy. Here, we developed a noninvasive physicochemical platform combining hyaluronic acid (HA)-functionalized paclitaxel-loaded solid lipid nanoparticles (SLNs) with high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) for localized melanoma therapy. The optimized SLNs exhibited a hydrodynamic diameter of 134.6 ± 4.2 nm and a zeta potential of –22.3 ± 1.5 mV. HIFU induced changes in the structural organization of the lipid matrix, accelerating paclitaxel release and enhancing skin penetration. In vitro, SLNs with HIFU reduced B16F10 melanoma cell viability to below 20% while maintaining approximately 65% viability of HaCaT keratinocytes. The combined treatment increased intracellular ROS generation by 6.2-fold and enhanced apoptotic signaling. In ex vivo porcine skin, HIFU-assisted delivery of coumarin-6-loaded SLNs increased fluorescence penetration to approximately 1500 μm, compared with 750 μm without HIFU. In B16F10 tumor-bearing mice, topical SLNs combined with HIFU under mild hyperthermia (41–43 °C) achieved 90.1% tumor growth inhibition at Day 8, 81.5% tumor necrosis, and 86.5% TUNEL-positive cells without significant body-weight loss or treatment-related toxicity. These findings support HIFU-enhanced SLNs as a potential strategy for improving cutaneous paclitaxel delivery and suppressing localized melanoma growth.

title: In Situ Synthesis of Quantum Dot–Polymer Nanocomposites: Mechanisms, Interfacial Engineering, and Optoelectronic Applications
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Quantum dot (QD)–polymer nanocomposites have emerged as promising optoelectronic materials for next-generation technologies, including high-performance displays, photovoltaics, optical sensing, and bioimaging systems. Nevertheless, conventional physical blending strategies for fabricating QD–polymer composites face critical limitations such as environmentally unfriendly processing protocols, aggregation-induced fluorescence quenching, and compromised photoluminescence stability, which collectively hinder their practical implementation.
