In situ synthesis of QDs within polymer matrices has recently emerged as a transformative methodology to address these challenges. This comprehensive review systematically examines three categories of in situ synthesized QDs (II–VI, IV–VI, and perovskite nanostructures) within diverse polymeric architectures, including conventional thermoplastics, block copolymers, and conjugated polymers. A critical analysis is presented on how polymer composition (e.g., functional groups and chain mobility) and nanostructural design (e.g., micellar confinement and template-directed assembly) govern the nucleation kinetics, crystallographic features, and optoelectronic properties of QDs. The review further highlights cutting-edge applications spanning ultrasensitive chemical detection, multimodal bioimaging platforms, and high-color-purity QD-LED displays. Finally, we discuss fundamental challenges and propose strategic directions for scalable manufacturing, focusing on interface engineering and stability enhancement. With the advent of solution-processable polymer platforms and precision nanofabrication techniques, in situ QD–polymer nanocomposite synthesis is poised to bridge the gap between laboratory innovation and industrial-scale production in optoelectronic device manufacturing.

title: Food-Grade Hyaluronidase-Driven Janus Zein Nanomotors for Targeted Curcumin Delivery in Colorectal Microenvironments
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Curcumin, a bioactive polyphenol, exhibits high therapeutic potential, but its poor solubility and bioavailability restrict its application. Furthermore, conventional nanocarriers face cumbersome fabrication, poor biocompatibility, and insufficient tumor extracellular matrix penetration. Here, we constructed a hyaluronidase-driven, curcumin-loaded food-grade Janus zein nanomotor (HAase-CZ-JNs) via Pickering emulsion templating and genipin crosslinking. Its asymmetric "half-hydrophilic, half-hydrophobic" topology minimizes mass transfer resistance and stabilizes the enzyme's active conformation, boosting immobilized HAase catalytic efficiency (kcat/Km) 4.01-fold over free enzyme. Driven by endogenous HA, HAase-CZ-JNs exhibit robust substrate-dependent self-propulsion (effective diffusion coefficient: 63.69 μm2/s), 8.2-fold higher than that of fully modified nanoparticles (HAase-CZ-NPs). In vitro, these nanomotors actively penetrate dense 3D spheroids, enhancing deep cytotoxicity against HT-29 cells (IC50 = 1.364 μg/mL) with a 12-h core-killing efficacy 7.9-fold greater than HAase-CZ-NPs. Utilizing biosafe natural materials, this system offers a promising nanokinetic strategy for targeted curcumin delivery in colorectal microenvironments.

title: Supramolecular Matrine-Proanthocyanidins Nanocomplex-Integrated Carboxymethyl Chitosan Hydrogel with Phenylboronic Acid Modification for Atopic Dermatitis Therapy
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease featured by immune dysregulation, oxidative stress, and an impaired epidermal barrier. Oxidative stress and inflammation establish a self-sustaining vicious cycle that accelerates the progression of atopic dermatitis. However, few naturally derived self-assembled nanohydrogels have been developed to disrupt this reciprocal loop for the treatment of cutaneous AD. In this study, matrine (MAT) and proanthocyanidins (PAC), two Chinese medicine-derived molecules with inherent antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities, co-assembled spontaneously into nanoparticles (PM NPs) in aqueous solution. Incorporation of PM NPs into the phenylboronic acid-modified carboxymethyl chitosan (CP) crosslinked network enhanced the mechanical strength of carboxymethyl chitosan, forming a composite hydrogel (CPPM). Spectral results verified that PM NP self-assembly was mediated by hydrogen bonding and π-π stacking. CPPM efficiently scavenged reactive oxygen species (ROS), suppressed the activation of the Ox-CaMKII and NF-κB signaling pathways, and activated Nrf2 to restore epidermal redox homeostasis. CPPM exhibited favorable moisturizing capacity, appropriate rheological properties, and mild ROS-triggered release to realize local therapeutic effects. In 1-chloro-2,4-dinitrochlorobenzene (DNCB)-induced AD mice, topical CPPM application significantly alleviated epidermal hyperplasia, itching, and inflammatory cytokine expression without obvious toxicity. This self-assembled bioactive hydrogel can concurrently regulate oxidative stress and inflammatory responses, offering a promising topical therapeutic approach against AD.

title: A Multifunctional Core–Sheath Fiber Patch Based on Cellulose Nanocrystal-Reinforced and Curcumin-Loaded Polylactic Acid for Enhanced Pelvic Tissue Repair
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Pelvic organ prolapse (POP) affects millions of women due to tissue defect, marked by disrupted collagen homeostasis and abnormal immune reaction. Therefore, there is a demand for developing a multifunctional patch resolving these current straits. Herein, we fabricated a multifunctional core–sheath fibrous patch via coaxial electrospinning, comprising cellulose nanocrystal (CNC)-reinforced polylactic acid (PLA) sheath and curcumin-loaded PLA core. Post-electrospinning heat treatment enhanced PLA crystallinity improved mechanical properties and enabled sustained curcumin release. The patch exhibited stable degradation, good biocompatibility, and potent anti-inflammatory activity. In vivo, the CNC-PLA/Cur-h patch achieved native-tissue-comparable biomechanical strength within 4 weeks, with enhanced neovascularization, elevated collagen I/III ratio, and well-organized extracellular matrix. RNA sequencing confirmed upregulated angiogenesis and ECM-related genes, as well as downregulated inflammatory markers. This multifunctional platform integrates mechanical robustness, controlled biodegradability, and proregenerative capacity, presenting a promising strategy for POP repair.

title: High-Performance Ionic Thermoelectric Conversion toward Self-powered Human–Computer Interaction
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ion thermoelectric conversion has great potential for application in thermoelectric energy harvesting and self-powered devices due to its high ionic Seebeck coefficient. However, existing systems generally suffer from problems such as low thermoelectric conversion efficiency, insufficient mechanical properties, and difficulty in assembling functional devices. Here, we report a novel ionic thermoelectric hydrogel based on a sodium alginate–polyacrylamide dual network with zirconium oxychloride as the electrolyte. The hydrogel achieves a tensile strength of 44.77 kPa and an elongation at break of 327.64%. Simultaneously, a crosslinked structure with ion transport pathways is formed, providing continuous pathways for the differential dissociation and migration of Zr(IV)-containing species and free Cl– ions, thereby enhancing ion thermodiffusion. This yields an ionic Seebeck coefficient as high as –14 mV K–1. A single ionic thermoelectric hydrogel generates 56 mV at ΔT = 4 K, while four hydrogels connected in series produce an output voltage of approximately 0.2 V, demonstrating the feasibility of hydrogel array integration for practical applications. Through series integration, voltage boosting, and capacitive energy storage, a self-powered system for gesture recognition and drone control is successfully constructed. The integrated equipment drives a low-power microprocessor and gesture recognition module, enabling real-time interactive control for raise-to-fly. This work provides a strategy for high-performance, integrable, and environmentally stable ionic thermoelectric devices, advancing their practical applications in self-powered systems and human–machine interaction.

title: Conductive MOF Heterostructures with Enhanced Interfacial Charge Transfer and Improved Humidity Tolerance for Superior Room-Temperature H2S Detection
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Conductive metal–organic frameworks (C-MOFs) have emerged as promising candidates for room-temperature chemical sensing due to their intrinsic conductivity and tunable structures. However, their practical application is still hindered by limited sensitivity and poor humidity tolerance. In this work, CuO nanoparticles were introduced onto Co-HHTP nanorods to construct interfacial heterojunctions, followed by hydrophobic ZIF-8 modification to regulate gas–surface interactions. The optimized Cu10Co-HHTP sensor exhibited a high response of 15.8 toward 50 ppm H2S, excellent selectivity, and a low detection limit of 24 ppb at room temperature. Although ZIF-8 modification slightly reduced the H2S response, it substantially enhanced the humidity tolerance, decreasing the response loss at 85% RH from 59.1% to 18.4% relative to that at 33% RH. Experimental characterizations and density functional theory calculations revealed that the CuO/Co-HHTP heterointerface promotes charge redistribution and enhances H2S adsorption, while the hydrophobic ZIF-8 layer weakens the interaction between H2O and the outer surface, thereby suppressing competitive water adsorption and alleviating humidity-induced interference. These findings demonstrate that combining heterojunction engineering with hydrophobic surface regulation provides an effective strategy for the development of high-performance C-MOF-based gas sensors for reliable room-temperature operation with improved sensitivity and environmental stability.

title: Atom-Economic Intramolecular Rearrangement Enables High-Film-Retention Non-chemically Amplified Resists for Advanced Lithography
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The transition to high-numerical-aperture (High-NA) extreme ultraviolet lithography (EUVL) imposes stringent constraints on resist film thickness, posing a critical challenge in terms of maintaining film thickness consistency to ensure pattern fidelity during subsequent etching processes. Herein, we introduce a molecular design strategy that intrinsically addresses this issue by employing an atom-conservative photochemical reaction. A series of non-chemically amplified resists (n-CARs) based on ortho-nitrobenzaldehyde (o-NBA)-modified PMMA polymers (PoMA) were developed. Distinct from conventional resists that suffer from decomposition-induced thickness loss, PoMA leverages a unique intramolecular rearrangement mechanism. Upon exposure, the o-NBA moieties undergo an intramolecular photorearrangement into ortho-nitrosobenzoic acid (o-NSBA), inducing a polarity switch for negative-tone development (NTD) without mass loss. Consequently, the PoMA resists exhibited near-quantitative film retention after exposure and development. By tuning the molecular weight of PoMA, we optimized the delicate balance between sensitivity and resolution, achieving 18 nm half-pitch (HP) resolution with a line edge roughness (LER) of 1.7 nm in electron beam lithography (EBL) and 30 nm HP with 2.5 nm LER in EUVL. Furthermore, etch resistance and pattern transfer capability into silicon at feature sizes down to 25 nm HP were also demonstrated. These findings highlight the atom-economic rearrangement strategy as a promising paradigm for designing photoresists for advanced lithography, effectively addressing the critical issue of film thickness loss in ultrathin resist layers.

title: Assessing the carbon emissions and energy consumption of US hyperscale data centres
abstract: The growing number of hyperscale data centres raises concerns about their environmental impacts. This study presents a facility-resolved attributional framework to assess the carbon footprint of hyperscale data centres in the USA using plant-level electricity-generation and emissions data.

title: Leveraging sequence purification for accurate prediction of multiple conformational states with AlphaFold2
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: AlphaFold2 (AF2) has transformed protein structure prediction by harnessing co-evolutionary constraints embedded in multiple sequence alignments (MSAs). MSAs not only encode static structural information, but also contain evolutionary signatures linked to protein dynamics and conformational heterogeneity, which are central to biological function. However, the subtle co-evolutionary signals that bias proteins toward distinct conformational states are often obscured by noise within MSA data and remain challenging to decipher. Here, we introduce AF-ClaSeq, a systematic framework that enriches and purifies state-specific evolutionary signals through iterative sequence classification and selection. By identifying sequence subsets that preferentially encode distinct conformational states, AF-ClaSeq enables robust predictions of alternative conformations across diverse protein systems. Our findings indicate that the accuracy of alternative-state prediction depends more on the purity of the evolutionary signal within an MSA than on sequence depth. Notably, purified sequences encoding specific structural states are distributed across phylogenetic clades and superfamilies, rather than being confined to individual lineages. By extending AF2 beyond single-state structure prediction, AF-ClaSeq provides a promising approach for exploring protein structural plasticity, establishing a foundation for future studies of the sequence determinants underlying conformational switching and allosteric regulation.

title: 4D mitochondrial network assumes distinct and predictive phenotypes through human lung and intestinal epithelial development
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Mitochondria form dynamic three-dimensional networks that exhibit a wide range of morphology and motility depending on cell state, cell type, and cell fate. Isolated phenotypes have been described for individual cell states, but how mitochondrial morphology and motility change across the full course of human tissue development has so far been unclear. Human stem cell-derived branching lung and intestinal organoids mimic developing human organs and make these systems accessible. Here we show, by imaging at key developmental time points from human stem cell through mature organoid tissue with lattice light-sheet microscopy, that mitochondrial networks adopt morphology and motility signatures that vary with developmental stage, that mitochondrial and cellular features can be used to predict developmental stage, and that two-dimensional measurements obscure features resolved only in three dimensions over time, yielding an integrated map of mitochondrial phenotypes across human tissue development.

title: Identification and deployment of a wild soybean FD allele for high-density planting and increased yield
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Shortened internode length is a key agronomic trait that optimizes crop architecture and promotes adaptability to high-density planting. Loci that confer short internodes while increasing yield remain scarce in soybean. Here, using chromosome segment-substitution lines, we identify the REDUCED INTERNODE 2 (RIN2) locus, which encodes the basic leucine zipper (bZIP) transcription factor FDc1 that exerts a negative regulatory effect on internode length. The RIN2ZYD06 allele from wild soybean has a strong ability to suppress internode elongation compared to RIN2SN14 allele from cultivated soybean. The RIN2SN14 promoter exhibits lower expression than that of RIN2ZYD06, thereby fostering internode elongation. RIN2 binds to and activates the STF1 and STF2 promoters, the proteins of which in turn promote gibberellin catabolism in the shoot apex to reduce internode elongation. Dt1, which confers stem-growth habit, physically interacts with RIN2, attenuating RIN2-mediated transcriptional regulation. STF1/2 act downstream of Dt1 and RIN2. At field locations, RIN2ZYD06 confers increased yield per plant and per plot at high planting densities. Taken together, we elucidate the molecular mechanism of RIN2 regulating internode length and identify a wild allele that optimizes soybean architecture for high-density planting.

title: A redox-coupled ROMO1–LONP1–SIRT3 axis controls hepatic lipid catabolism
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Disturbed balance between lipid anabolism and catabolism drives hepatic steatosis. Mitochondria play a central role in lipid clearance through free fatty acid (FFA) oxidation, yet the molecular mechanisms governing this metabolic process remain incompletely understood. Here, we establish ROMO1, a recently identified mitochondrial thiol-protector, as a critical regulator of mitochondrial FFA oxidation through the LONP1–SIRT3 signaling axis. Hepatocyte-specific ablation of ROMO1 impairs mitochondrial FFA oxidation and causes hepatic lipid accumulation. Mechanistically, ROMO1 loss induces sulfenylation of the mitochondrial protease LONP1, resulting in excessive degradation of SIRT3 and consequent hyperacetylation of mitochondrial proteins involved in FFA oxidation. Importantly, ROMO1 overexpression protects against hepatic steatosis and liver injury by suppressing LONP1 sulfenylation and preserving SIRT3 protein stability in multiple mouse models of steatotic liver disease, whereas ROMO1 deficiency exacerbates disease progression. Moreover, spontaneous fatty liver in aged rhesus macaques is associated with reduced ROMO1 expression and concomitant loss of SIRT3 protein. Collectively, our findings establish the ROMO1–LONP1–SIRT3 axis as a redox-coupled signaling cascade that links mitochondrial redox regulation to hepatic lipid catabolism, providing potential therapeutic targets for steatotic liver diseases.

title: Co-deficiency of RECQL1 and BLM causes replication stress associated with DNA damage and cohesion loss
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The mechanistic basis for chromosomal instability characteristic of RECQ helicase disorders remains poorly understood due to their molecular-genetic complexity. To characterize the genetic interactions of RECQL1 (also referred to as RECQL or RECQ1), implicated in RECON syndrome, we performed an RNA interference screen and discovered a functional relationship with BLM, a gene that is mutated in Bloom syndrome. RECQL1/BLM co-deficient cells display pronounced replication stress, DNA damage accumulation, and chromosomal instability. Strikingly, RECQL1/BLM co-deficiency induces sister chromatid separation during metaphase suppressible by depletion of the cohesin unloader WAPL, suggesting that a threshold of replication stress in the genetically co-deficient cells disrupts cohesion. Primary embryonic fibroblasts from transgenic Blm-/-;Recql-/- mice recapitulate the sister chromatid separation phenotype and heightened replication stress observed for human cells. Our findings highlight the joint roles of RECQL1 and BLM in the replication stress response and their concurrent importance for maintenance of chromosomal stability even in the absence of exogenously induced DNA damage. Furthermore, we elucidated a genetic interaction in which sister chromatid cohesion is synergistically elevated by the loss of two conserved RECQ helicases encoded by genes in which mutations are linked to hereditary diseases that are not associated with sister chromatid cohesion defects. The findings presented provide insights into the genetic crosstalk of two prominent RECQ helicases with established importance in clinical diseases of genomic instability.

title: Unlocking sustainable thermoelectric generation with zinc antimonide
abstract: Thermoelectric technologies must balance conversion efficiency with resource sustainability. Here the authors demonstrate that eco-friendly zinc antimonide (ZnSb) is a viable materials choice, delivering ~8% efficiency alongside exceptional cost-effectiveness.

title: MyoGen: unified biophysical modeling of human neuromotor activity and resulting signals
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Understanding human motor control requires integrating cortical and spinal activity, muscle mechanics, and electrophysiology, which are typically studied in isolation. We present MyoGen, an open-source framework that unifies spinal circuitry, proprioceptive feedback, musculotendon dynamics, and multimodal electromyography generation. Using data-driven optimization benchmarked against human motor unit recordings, MyoGen produces motor unit population activity matching experimental discharge-rate distributions and variability across muscles. The framework generates decomposable surface and intramuscular electromyography, reproduces beta-band modulation of descending drive and its transformation into force, and implements key sensorimotor loop components. Dimensionality reduction of simulated agonist-antagonist electromyography reveals low-dimensional control manifolds consistent with recordings from able-bodied individuals and those with spinal cord injury. Here, we show that MyoGen provides a physiologically grounded simulation substrate, enabling systematic investigation of motor control principles, benchmarking of signal-processing algorithms, and exploration of experimentally inaccessible sensorimotor interactions.

title: Author Correction: Vulnerability to climate-driven pathogen-specific diarrheal diseases: secondary analysis from the Global Enteric Multicenter Study and Vaccine Impact on Diarrhea in Africa follow-up

title: Holistic evaluation for deployment
abstract: Thermoelectric technologies can convert waste heat directly into clean electricity, but high laboratory efficiency does not necessarily translate into practical deployment. By revisiting the long-neglected material zinc antimonide, researchers now show that strong thermoelectric performance can go hand in hand with affordability and sustainability.

title: Multifunctional Dendrimer Interlayers for Tin-Based Perovskite Solar Cells: Inducing Interfacial Dipoles and Suppressing Electrode Corrosion
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Tin-based perovskite solar cells (Sn-PSCs) offer eco-friendly optoelectronics but suffer from low efficiency and ambient instability. Here, we introduce a second-generation poly(amidoamine) (PAMAM) dendrimer interlayer between the C60/BCP electron transport layer and the Ag top electrode. Electrostatic field orientation induced by the metallic electrode activates a PAMAM dipole that shifts the effective interface work function by ∼0.55 eV. This modification of the interfacial energetics is accompanied by an increase in the open-circuit voltage (VOC) by ∼50 mV and is consistent with reduced contact-induced energetic losses. Additionally, the dendrimer forms a physical/chemical barrier against iodine-mediated electrode corrosion. Consequently, unencapsulated Sn-PSCs retain 80% of their initial power conversion efficiency (PCE) after 1000 h in ambient air (∼30 °C, 20–35% RH), a benchmark stability also demonstrated here for Sn–Pb PSCs. This electrode-induced dipole orientation presents a generalizable strategy for boosting efficiency and operational durability in lead-free perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Low-Temperature CO2 Desorption Enables Ammonium Carbonate Electrolysis Beyond pH Swing Limits
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Bipolar membrane (BPM) electrolysis enables direct conversion of carbon capture solutions to fuels, eliminating energy-intensive CO2 purification and compression. However, CO2 desorption from potassium carbonate limits Faradaic efficiency (FE), with a theoretical maximum CO FE of 50% due to stoichiometric constraints. Here, we examine aqueous ammonia as an alternative carbon capture solution, where CO2 desorption can be enhanced using low-grade waste heat. Gas-phase CO2 release from 1 M ammonium carbonate increases 7.7-fold from 20 to 65 °C, increasing CO FE from 32 to 53% at 100 mA cm–2. This enhancement is consistent with increased CO2 availability from temperature-sensitive NH3–CO2–H2O equilibria. Using a hydrophilic SiO2-decorated Ni single-atom catalyst, we achieve 84% CO FE at 100 mA cm–2 with 2 M ammonium carbonate at 50 °C and 3 bar. Integration with a carbon capture absorber enables stable operation and electrolyte recapture, establishing a closed-loop capture-conversion process.

title: From Nonstep to Step: Voltage‑Response‑Driven Interfacial Evolution and Closed‑Pore Sodium Filling in Hard Carbon Anode
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Hard carbon (HC) is regarded as the most commercially viable anode for sodium-ion batteries. However, during the initial discharge of the HC anode, the thick solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) derived from the decomposition of the ester-based electrolytes severely restricts sodium storage kinetics. Herein, we propose a customized discharge strategy that triggers a step voltage response (SR) in the HC anode to achieve rapid interfacial passivation. Through multiscale characterizations and theoretical calculations, we elucidate the underlying mechanism: the field-induced concentration effect within the interfacial electrolyte steers the decomposition pathways toward inorganic products, favoring the formation of a thin, uniform, and highly ionically conductive SEI. The accelerated interfacial kinetics significantly lowers the diffusion barrier, thereby enhancing the accessibility of closed pores for quasi-metallic sodium cluster storage. Consequently, the SR-treated HC anode delivers improved rate performance in both the sodium-ion full battery and hybrid capacitor. This study offers critical insights into the design of the formation protocol and provides a facile field-modulated strategy to enhance the sodium storage kinetics of the HC anode.

title: Extraction-Limited Charge Loss in Tin-Based Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Tin-based perovskite solar cells (PSCs) present a promising lead-free alternative for photovoltaics, yet their performance remains markedly inferior to that of lead-based counterparts. A limited understanding of the underlying differences in charge transport dynamics between tin- and lead-based PSCs continues to impede efforts to overcome the reduced open-circuit voltage (Voc) and fill factor (FF) characteristic of tin-based devices. Here, using bias-modulated electrical transient measurements, we reveal a previously neglected extraction-limited charge loss mechanism in tin-based PSCs (efficiency > 14%) that is not evident in lead-based counterparts (> 25%) and fundamentally constrains both Voc and FF. Under high forward bias, the defects and their associated self-doping at the perovskite/electron transport layer interface severely reduce charge extraction efficiency by limiting the extraction of low-mobility carriers due to bulk field screening, which in turn leads to reduced collection efficiency as the unextracted carriers are forced into nonradiative recombination. This mechanism explains the low Voc and FF in tin-based PSCs and underscores interfacial doping control as critical for further performance enhancement.

title: A precommissural nucleus-cingulate circuit coordinates a stress-induced agitation-like state
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Agitation combines motor restlessness with negative affect, yet the neural circuits coordinating these features remain unclear. We establish a chronic conditioned stress paradigm in mice that evokes a context-dependent agitation-like state marked by increased walking, reduced digging, altered bout kinematics and aversion, distinct from escape-like flight. Conditioned stress recruits predominantly glutamatergic cholecystokinin (CCK)-expressing neurons in the precommissural nucleus (Prc) and enhances their responses to conditioned cues. Projection screening identifies cingulate cortex area 2 (Cg2) as a behaviorally enriched output. Bidirectional manipulations show that Prc-CCK neurons and their Cg2 terminals are both sufficient for and required for key motor and avoidance-related components of this state. Local CCK-B receptor signaling contributes to pathway-evoked behavior. Selected recruitment and activation effects extend to female mice, whereas chronic unpredictable stress and remote retrieval delineate behavioral and temporal boundaries. Here, we show that a diencephalic-cingulate pathway coordinates stress-associated motor restlessness with negative valence.

title: A Metal–Organic Framework-on-Metal–Organic Framework Chemical Nose for Intelligent Identification of Depression-Related Biomarkers via Machine Learning
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Depression is a complex mental disorder associated with dysregulation of multiple neurotransmitter-related biomarkers, including Try, 5-HT, 5-HIAA, and 5-HTP. Herein, we report a MOF-on-MOF fluorescent sensor array, RhB@ZIF-8-on-FL@UiO-67, for simultaneous discrimination and detection of these biomarkers. Spatial separation of dyes within the hierarchical architecture effectively suppresses fluorescence crosstalk and generates multiple independent luminescent channels, enhancing signal diversity and sensing performance. The resulting multidimensional fluorescence responses enable accurate identification of Try, 5-HT, 5-HIAA, 5-HTP, and their mixtures. Both LDA and HCA achieved a classification accuracy of 100% for the tested samples. Furthermore, machine learning models, including BP, RF, DT, SVM, and KNN, confirmed the robustness of the sensing platform. This work integrates MOF-on-MOF engineering with machine learning-assisted pattern recognition, offering a sensitive and reliable strategy for multiplex biomarker analysis and providing a promising approach for intelligent diagnosis of complex diseases.

title: Hazardous glacial lakes need reservoir governance
abstract: Climate warming is expanding thousands of glacial lakes with unstable natural dams, yet high-risk lakes remain outside formal safety oversight despite their potential for downstream harm. These lakes need consequence-based governance analogous to engineered dams and reservoirs, beginning with risk-tiered monitoring and clearer protection during conflict.

title: Burst-like intracellular antibody infusion via membrane-permeabilizing peptide microcondensates
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Intracellular antibody delivery enables modulation of challenging intracellular targets, including intrinsically disordered proteins, and holds considerable promise for biomedical applications. Here we show that microcondensates composed of engineered IgGs bearing glutamic acid– and tyrosine-containing tag sequences together with a trimeric membrane-permeabilizing L17E peptide [FcB(L17E)3] enable burst-like, rapid intracellular infusion of IgG antibodies under physiological salt and serum conditions. Dynamic membrane remodeling, including filopodia-like protrusions that internalize microcondensates, is visualized by lattice light-sheet and electron microscopy. The recruitment of the intrinsically disordered protein TDP-43 to stress granules is markedly inhibited by treatment with a TDP-43-targeting IgG. Physicochemical factors governing the ability of microcondensates to mediate intracellular IgG infusion are also investigated.

title: Structural Engineering of Bio-Alkaloid Ionic Liquid-Mesoporous Silica Nanohybrids for Optimized Transdermal Atopic Dermatitis Therapy
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) are highly promising drug carriers owing to their exceptionally large surface area and tailorable pore structures for high drug-loading capacity, but their transdermal delivery is severely restricted by the skin barrier. Integrating natural ionic liquids (ILs) can modulate skin permeability; however, the mechanistic impact of distinct IL molecular structures on the interfacial properties of MSN-IL nanohybrids remains poorly understood. In this study, we engineered a structure-specific transdermal delivery platform by assembling citric acid-functionalized MSNs with various natural bio-alkaloid cations (choline, L-carnitine, and matrine). Density functional theory (DFT) and macroscopic physicochemical evaluations revealed that the matrine-based system (CA-M 1:2) forms a highly stable, tight ion-pairing conformation. This specific configuration endows the formulated MSN-IL nanohybrid with a robust dynamic viscosity, providing effective steric occlusion to prevent premature drug leakage within the MSN pores. Despite this internal cohesion, in vitro assays and transmission electron microscopy confirmed that the CA-M 1:2 hybrid dynamically facilitated the highest transdermal flux, transporting intact MSNs across the skin barrier via an IL-associated enhancement of skin permeation. In the atopic dermatitis mouse model, topical treatment with the optimized DEX/MSN-IL system significantly accelerated lesion resolution, restored epidermal architecture, and suppressed inflammatory cascades by downregulating IFN-γ, TNF-α, and IgE levels. This work establishes a physical chemistry-driven molecular-to-macro framework for the rational design of structure-specific nanohybrids, advancing high-performance topical therapeutics for inflammatory skin diseases.

title: Impedance Matching Optimization and Meta-Structure Design of 3D-Printed Ion-Enhanced Hydrogels for Broadband and Strong Absorption of the Electromagnetic Wave
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Flexible hydrogels endowed with highly tunable 3D network architectures and multiple dielectric loss mechanisms hold tremendous application potential in electromagnetic wave (EMW) protection for wearable devices and conformally curved surfaces. Compared with conventional mold-casting fabrication, photocuring-based 3D printing enables the precise construction of complex macroscopic hydrogel geometries, including periodic arrays, lattice configurations, and gradient structures, thereby facilitating the synergistic optimization of structural design and microwave absorption performance. Herein, a series of ion-enhanced hydrogels were fabricated via digital light processing (DLP) 3D printing. The incorporation of metal cations simultaneously enhanced the dielectric response and optimized impedance matching, while markedly improving the elastic modulus by 215.2% and the volumetric toughness by 305.5%. Among these, the glycerol-modified hydrogel achieved an effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 8.17 GHz at a thickness of only 2.39 mm, and at the same thickness, the pure hydrogel failed to achieve effective absorption across the entire frequency range. Furthermore, after meta-structure design, the CST simulation results show that the ion-enhanced hydrogel delivered dual intense absorption peaks of –27.68 and –26.37 dB, with the EAB broadened to 14.0 GHz, fully covering both X and Ku-bands. Overall, this work provides a novel design strategy for developing high-performance flexible microwave absorbers that simultaneously possess printability and broadband absorption capability.

title: Self-Gelling Powdered Hydrogel Dressing Based on Dynamic Ion-Cross-Linked Natural Polypeptides for Shape-Adaptive Hemostasis and Accelerated Wound Healing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Effective hemorrhage control and wound closure are frequently compromised by the poor shape adaptability of preformed bulk hydrogel dressings, which fail to maintain intimate contact with irregular, bleeding tissue. To address this, we developed a freeze-dried polyelectrolyte complex powder (GLF-K) composed of dopamine-grafted γ-poly-l-glutamic acid, ε-poly-l-lysine, keratin, and iron ions. The network architecture relies on primary electrostatic cross-linking, synergistically reinforced by dopamine-Fe3+ coordination, which enables the GLF-K powder to rapidly rehydrate and transition into a cohesive hydrogel upon exposure to moisture. Compared to commercial chitosan hemostats, the GLF-K powder exhibited comparable or enhanced hemostatic efficacy in both in vitro and in vivo hemorrhage models, alongside excellent biocompatibility. More importantly, in a full-thickness skin defect model, GLF-K treatment accelerated the early-stage healing rate to 55.8% by day 3, significantly outperforming the control group. These findings suggest that GLF-K powder represents a promising integrated platform for managing acute hemorrhage and promoting expedited wound healing in irregular tissue defects.

title: Bio-Inspired Photothermal-Responsive P(NIPAM -co- NaAMPS)@SWCNT-COOH Hydrogel with Donnan-Driven Salt Rejection for High-Rate Solar Water Purification
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The global water shortage and pollution crisis motivates the development of high-efficiency, durable water remediation technologies. Solar-driven interfacial evaporation attracts broad interest for its high efficiency and environmental friendliness; nevertheless, vaporization-related latent-heat loss and salt accumulation severely restrict practical water-purification performance. Inspired by biological mechanisms, we report a thermoresponsive hydrogel evaporator based on poly(N-isopropylacrylamide-co-sodium 2-acrylamido-2-methyl-1-propanesulfonate) (P(NIPAM-co-NaAMPS)) composite network. Sulfonate groups (–SO3−) from NaAMPS impart high hydrophilicity to accelerate water uptake, while local Donnan equilibrium within the network suppresses salt ingress and accumulation. Under 1 sun irradiation (1 kW·m−2), PNIPAM-derived thermoresponsiveness triggers hydrophilic-to-hydrophobic chain collapse above the lower critical solution temperature (LCST). Upon photothermal contraction, the hydrogel achieves a stable-release water-purification rate of 9.87 ± 0.19 kg·m−2·h−1 (photothermal efficiency of 96.6%) during the 0.7 h plateau, alongside a cycle-averaged productivity of 0.87 ± 0.07 kg·m−2·h−1 over the full 9.0 h absorption-release cycle. Different from reported Donnan-type salt-rejection hydrogels, thermoresponsive draw agents, and polyelectrolyte evaporators, our innovation lies in coupling photothermally activated liquid-water extrusion with Donnan-mediated salt rejection, instead of simple material blending. The hydrogel maintains good stability across 30 cycles in 3.5 wt % saline water, showing promise for partial-salt-rejection pretreatment of brackish and diluted seawater. This work provides a strategy for cyclically stable solar water purification combining salt rejection and contaminant removal.

title: Understanding the Role of Solid Polymer Electrolyte Network Structure and Modulus in In Situ Anode Formation of “Anode-Free” Sodium Metal Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract “Anode-free” solid-state battery concepts based on sodium metal have attracted greater research interest recently due to their potential economic advantages, namely lower material costs and simplified, less expensive processing. However, these cell concepts suffer from poor cycling reversibility and cycle life, and little is understood about the fundamentals that govern sodium metal growth during in situ anode formation in solid-state batteries (SSBs). In this work, we use two model cross-linked network solid polymer electrolyte systems with varying cross-link density and modulus to investigate how such properties influence sodium metal growth and cycling stability. Using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, we show that solid polymer electrolyte (SPE) modulus strongly influences the early-stage morphology and charge-transfer kinetics of in situ formed sodium metal anodes. The higher-modulus SPE promotes faster in-plane growth of sodium metal, particularly during the early stages of in situ anode formation. Consequently, the higher-modulus SPE displays 3.0× and 1.9× lower interfacial resistances than the lower-modulus SPE at plating capacities of 0.05 and 0.1 mAh cm–2, respectively. Despite lower interfacial resistance early in anode formation, the higher-modulus SPE displays shorter cycle life in Na|SPE|Cu “anode-free” half cells at 2.3 ± 1.1 mAh cm–2 compared to 6.6 ± 2.9 for the lower-modulus SPE. This work demonstrates that tuning SPE network structure through cross-link density can increase modulus and accelerate electroactive Na-SPE interface formation, but improved interfacial kinetics do not necessarily translate to greater long-term cycling stability. In situ indentation experiments in SEM showed that increasing cross-link density also yields a more brittle network that is more susceptible to crack propagation, which likely facilitates dendrite penetration and reduces cycle life.

title: Genetic variant that reshaped the human brain was inherited from Neanderthals
abstract: DNA derived from the ancient hominin might make parts of our brains smaller — and protect against schizophrenia.

title: Two-dimensional transport mechanisms in the vicinity of the X-points in snowflake divertors
abstract: Snowflake divertor (SFD) experiments show enhanced radial transport near the X-points, more than may be explained by standard two-dimensional edge transport models without drifts. Here we investigate transport mechanisms in SFDs through two complementary approaches: (i) modelling of recent SFD experiments performed at MAST-U with the edge transport code UEDGE with and drifts enabled, and (ii) reduced modelling of transport and turbulence in the vicinity of the X-points with a model developed here and implemented in BOUT++. Through these two approaches we assess the two leading candidates for this transport: equilibrium drifts driven by strong poloidal gradients near the primary X-point, and the ‘churning mode’ (CM), a toroidally-symmetric plasma vortex close to the X-points. UEDGE modelling shows that equilibrium drifts do play a role in increasing particle and energy transport across the primary separatrix, increasing the proportion of heat flux delivered to secondary strike points (SPs) and reducing peak heat fluxes at the primary SPs. This mechanism is less effective in the upper divertor due the reversed drift directions in combination with the device geometry. Including drifts in the model is also shown to improve agreement with the experimental radiated power profiles. To self-consistently compare the impact of drifts and the CM we develop a reduced-MHD model which includes both effects, and which is implemented in BOUT++. We find that equilibrium drifts are dominant when the ratio of plasma pressure in the null region to poloidal magnetic pressure at the midplane is low, , which were the conditions obtained in the MAST-U experiments. The CM was found to be dominant for , leading to increased transport across the null region and activation of secondary divertor legs.

title: A near-quantum-limited diamond maser amplifier operating at millikelvin temperatures
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Current microwave quantum technologies require the amplification of weak signals with minimal added noise at millikelvin temperatures. To date, this stringent requirement has been met exclusively by superconducting technologies, such as Josephson or kinetic-inductance parametric amplifiers. A fundamentally distinct alternative approach could be offered by masers, the microwave counterpart of lasers, which were predicted as early as the 1950s to achieve quantum-limited noise performance under ideal conditions. However, their dependence on cryogenic operation historically limited further advancement. Here we demonstrate the first-ever non-superconducting, near-quantum-limited maser amplifier operating at millikelvin temperatures utilising nitrogen impurity spins (P1 centres) in diamond. Population inversion is achieved via microwave pumping, exploiting a four-spin cross-relaxation mechanism. We realise a maximum power gain exceeding 30 dB, an added noise of approximately 2.55 quanta above the standard quantum limit, and a maximum 1 dB output compression point of −63 dBm at 6.595 GHz. The ability to operate in strong static magnetic fields of arbitrary orientation may offer a complementary, non-superconducting route for applications such as semiconducting spin-qubit readout, magnetic-resonance spectroscopy, and dark-matter axion searches.

title: n = 1 ideal MHD stability of tokamak plasmas with low aspect ratio and negative triangularity
abstract: Spherical tokamaks (STs) exhibit good ideal magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) stability owing to their low-aspect-ratio configuration, while negative triangularity (NT) configurations have recently attracted considerable attention for their superior confinement performance, despite their inferior MHD stability. To evaluate whether these two advantageous regimes can be reconciled, we investigate the ideal no-wall MHD stability of NT configurations at low aspect ratios. Using the CHEASE+MARS code suite, we perform beta limit scans over various triangularity and aspect ratio values, with prescribed safety factor profiles and normalized pressure gradient profiles, which provides a controlled comparison. The results show that, at lower aspect ratios, the stability of positive triangularity (PT) configurations is enhanced, consistent with classical expectations; whereas counter-intuitively, the stability of NT configurations deteriorates. We present several physical interpretations of this phenomenon, both qualitatively (‘good/bad curvature’) and quantitatively (magnetic well depth and Mercier criterion), and show that they are consistent with the calculated trend. In addition, the stabilizing effect of the safety factor is preserved at low aspect ratios for both PT and NT configurations, partially mitigating the aforementioned stability deterioration of NT plasmas.

title: Encapsulating an iron complex within a heme and anthraquinone codecorated capsule for multiphoton C(sp3)−H bond oxygenation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The allosteric effect in proteins controls biological function omnipotently, but simulating both the regulatory functions and catalytic processes of analogues faces marked challenges. By encapsulating a non-heme FeIII-complex into the cavity of an anthraquinone and heme co-decorated coordination capsule, herein we report a light-responsive allosteric catalysis for activating O2 and metabolizing C(sp3)−H bonds. Light irradiation initially triggers the bridged FeIII-porphyrins switching into unbridged FeII/O=FeIV-porphyrin pair for substrate oxygenation. Parallelly exciting the anthraquinone groups sensitizes O2 to 1O2 via energy transfer, meanwhile exciting the non-heme FeIII-complexes generates the chlorine radicals via ligand-to-metal charge transfer. The capsules enforce heme and non-heme FeII fragments into proximity, forming an Fe−O − O−Fe intermediate with the reactive 1O2 species for O − O bond cleavage. Synergistic hydrogen abstraction by chlorine radicals and O=FeIV-porphyrin by combining multiple photons selectively and fleetly oxygenates thioxanthene to thioxanthen-9-one within the capsule pocket, therefore reshaping oxygenase for selective metabolism in a supramolecular approach.

title: Brønsted/Lewis acid-catalyzed divergent cascade cyclization of alkoxyallene for the total synthesis of eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloids
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloids are two types of biogenetically related polycyclic monoterpenoid alkaloids with distinct structural features. Reported synthetic strategies typically construct the core architectures of eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloids independently, and no protocol enabling their simultaneous synthesis has yet been developed. Herein, we describe the assembly of both eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloid skeletons from a common alkoxyallene precursor, a characteristic that aligns with their inherent biogenetic connection. Our investigations reveal that upon Prins-type spirocyclization of the alkoxyallene under Brønsted or Lewis acid catalysis, the intermediate undergoes two discrete tandem reaction pathways: Mannich-like cyclization/migration to construct the skeleton of eburnane alkaloids under Brønsted acid catalysis, whereas nucleophilic addition to the indole iminium assembles the aspidofractinine alkaloids framework under Lewis acid catalysis. The developed divergent cascade cyclization strategy has been successfully applied to the total synthesis of eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloids including (−)-eburnamonine, (−)-eburnamenine, (+)-eburnamine, and (±)-aspidofractinine.

title: Improving molecular property prediction with score-based diffusion models
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: We explore diffusion-based training as a flexible approach to molecular property prediction in settings shaped by chemical, biophysical, and latent heterogeneity. To address this, we build on score-based generative diffusion models and introduce a conditional diffusion module for predictive tasks, equipped with a joint training and sampling guidance scheme and an optional gated residual mechanism that regulates feature- vs target-driven information flow across noise levels. The module acts as a plug-in learning block for existing molecular encoders, making it complementary to advances in representation learning. Across diverse feature extractors and graph neural networks, diffusion-based training improves over conventional maximum-likelihood objectives on small-molecule regression benchmarks and matches or exceeds strong baselines on multitask regression and classification datasets. It also produces well-calibrated predictive uncertainty as measured by prediction interval coverage, enables confidence-guided ranking, and performs well in challenging settings including activity cliffs and class-imbalanced multitask prediction. Overall, these results position diffusion as a promising representation-agnostic approach for effective molecular property prediction.

title: Knowledge-guided machine learning deciphers spatiotemporal dynamics in chemical reactor systems
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Characterizing the spatiotemporal dynamics of complex chemical reactors, especially localized engineering-critical points or regions, remains challenging in process engineering. Although data-driven methods offer computational advantages, the incorporation of domain-specific physical knowledge can further enhance their predictive performance. Here, we present a physics-informed machine learning framework that systematically embeds coking mechanisms and heat transfer principles into neural network architecture and training constraints. Using a coke-accumulating cracking reactor as a prototypical case, the proposed approach reproduces the spatiotemporal distributions of key operational parameters obtained from conventional simulations with high fidelity and achieves a 105-fold computational acceleration. Crucially, the incorporation of mechanistic knowledge enhances prediction fidelity for critical safety indicators, particularly the maximum external wall temperature (error

title: Structurally guided wavefront neural encoder for broad-range generalizable 3D holography
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Deep learning has advanced computer-generated holography, but learned models remain coupled to fixed wavelengths and distances, limiting generalization. Here we present the structurally guided wavefront neural encoder (SGWN-Encoder), which integrates diffraction physics with neural networks and employs a structural propagation strategy that analytically strips the parameter-sensitive global phase. This reveals a scale-normalized description of diffraction, letting the network learn transferable light-field evolution rules and generalize across propagation distances and visible wavelengths by direct inference. A dataset-free paradigm built on statistically diverse random fields teaches the model the structural mapping from complex amplitude to phase-only holograms instead of external image distributions. Without fine-tuning, a single SGWN-Encoder maintains a distance-averaged RGB PSNR of 31.9 dB and SSIM of 0.91 over the primary 2–200 mm range, retaining reconstruction up to 500 mm. Numerical and optical experiments on full-color 3D scenes establish a physically grounded route toward adaptive holographic displays.

title: In-situ fabrication of ultra-conformal nanomesh epidermal sensors on arbitrary skin surface
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Recent advances in soft electronics have enabled the conformal integration of epidermal sensors on skin, significantly improving performance, long-term stability, and user comfort. However, achieving perfect conformability between conventional planar devices and three-dimensional skin surfaces remains a major challenge due to possible Gaussian curvature mismatch. In this study, we propose in situ fabrication of conductive nanofibres to achieve conformal epidermal sensors on arbitrary surfaces. We develop a stable and uniform carbon nanotube-based hybrid precursor for the fabrication of sub-1-μm intrinsically conductive nanofibres directly on skin, achieving conformability on both developable surfaces and non-developable surfaces. The porous nanomesh exhibits excellent gas-permeability, radiative heat dissipation efficiency, biocompatibility, and long-term stability, making it suitable for user-friendly epidermal electronics. We leverage this strategy to design and fabricate various conformal epidermal sensors, including electrophysiological sensor, electrodermal activity sensor, pressure sensor, and multi-channel sensor array for hand gesture recognition using deep learning algorithm, demonstrating its broad applicability.

title: Highly conductive halide Na-ion conductor enabled by cost-effective aliovalent carbonate polyanion substitution for all-solid-state sodium batteries
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Halide-based Na-ion conductors have attracted intense attention due to their favorable (electro)chemical compatibility with oxide positive electrodes. Among these, zirconium (Zr)-based halide solid electrolytes (SEs) offer a cost advantage over halide SEs based on rare metals, but the relatively low ionic conductivity has limited their application in all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs). Here, we report employing soda ash (Na2CO3) as a low-cost precursor to introduce an aliovalent carbonate polyanion and produce a family of Na-Zr-Cl-CO3 conductors with nominal compositions of (2-x)NaCl-xNa2CO3-ZrCl4. This substitution increases structural disorder and amorphization, creating structural environments that facilitate Na+ transport. At the optimal composition, its ionic conductivity reaches 1.02 mS cm−1 at 25 °C. The optimized Na-Zr-Cl-CO3 SE also exhibits stable electrochemical behavior and favorable mechanical properties. When paired with NaCrO2 positive electrode, the assembled ASSBs deliver an initial discharge capacity of 117 mAh g−1 at 0.1 C and demonstrate a long-term cycling stability at 0.3 C for 850 cycles. This work highlights carbonate polyanion substitution as a practical strategy for improving low-cost Zr-based halide SEs, offering a promising route toward ASSBs with high performance.

title: Continuous Molecular-Scale Welding of Carbon Nanotubes into Cellulose Yarns for Robust, Multisensory All-Textile Electronics
abstract: The seamless integration of electronic functionalities into sustainable textile architectures is foundational for next-generation wearable intelligence. However, achieving high electrical performance without compromising the inherent comfort and durability of natural fibers remains a persistent challenge. Herein, we report a continuous manufacturing strategy for robust conductive yarns via phosphoric acid-mediated molecular-scale welding technique. By precisely controlling the partial dissolution and in situ regeneration of cellulose chains, carbon nanotubes (CNTs) are architecturally “locked” within the reorganized molecular framework of yarns. This structural reconfiguration establishes a highly efficient, shielded charge transport network, yielding an outstanding electrical conductivity of 334.6 S m⁻1 at an ultralow CNT loading (11.2 wt%). The resulting Welded Cellulose/CNT Yarns (WCCYs) exhibit exceptional interfacial adhesion, delivering superior mechanical tenacity and laundry durability that surpass conventional coated fibers. Leveraging these synergistic properties, we demonstrate an all-textile, multisensory platform capable of concurrent, high-fidelity monitoring of biomechanical deformations, physiological signatures, and environmental stimuli (humidity and volatile organics). The WCCY-based system enables precise respiratory pattern tracking and fine-grained recognition of hand gestures, effectively bridging the gap between molecular-level materials design and large-scale, multifunctional smart wearable applications. This work offers a scalable and sustainable route for transitioning traditional textiles into sophisticated human–machine interfaces. Highlights:1 A continuous manufacturing strategy for robust conductive yarns is established via phosphoric acid-mediated molecular-scale welding technique.2 The synergistic effect of phosphoric acid molecular-scale welding and cellulose on the dispersion of carbon nanotubes leads to the robust dual-network topological entanglement with exceptional interfacial adhesion and washing durability.3 A single-component, multisensory all-textile platform is successfully integrated to monitor diverse biomechanical deformations, biophysical signatures, and environmental stimuli precisely and concurrently.

title: Mixed-dimensional complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor technology for high-performance integrated circuits
abstract: With the help of a hard mask technology and pre-deposition annealing process, two-dimensional single-crystal molybdenum disulfide n-type transistors and one-dimensional aligned carbon nanotube p-type transistors can be integrated to create a mixed-dimensional complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor technology.

title: Synthetic Pathway Modulation of Metal Organization in Multivariate Metal–Organic Frameworks
abstract: ABSTRACT Multivariate metal–organic frameworks (MTV MOFs) incorporate various metals and/or linkers within a periodic backbone, offering structural diversity and emergent functionalities. Typically, conventional one‐pot synthesis does not allow for any control over the spatial arrangement or sequencing of metals within the framework. Here, we present a synthetic strategy to alter metal arrangement in multimetallic MTV MOFs, yielding materials with nearly identical composition yet distinct properties. Using isostructural m CB‐Co and m CB‐Ni MOFs, we generate two MTV MOFs with different one‐dimensional Ni/Co arrangements, resulting in distinct semiconducting and magnetic properties. High‐resolution electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESI‐HRMS) reveals the formation of distinct precursor species in solution, suggesting that prenucleation chemistry influences the final metal arrangement. This work establishes a new approach for modulating metal arrangement in MTV MOFs, enabling tunable functional properties in multimetallic frameworks for applications in catalysis, electronics, and quantum materials.

title: Peak water: Trends in decoupling regional and global water use
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Water use for human activities, including food and fiber production, energy generation, and residential, commercial, and industrial supply, has grown significantly over the past century, driven by rising populations, expanding economic activity, and changes in technologies and consumer demands. Traditional water planning has long assumed that the demand for water, like other resource demands, will grow in perpetuity, shaping infrastructure development, land-use decisions, and water-system investments. However, recent data and analysis challenge this assumption, suggesting that total water use in certain regions and sectors has peaked or even begun to decline, despite continued population and economic growth. This paper’s primary contribution is to reevaluate the status of “peak water” and decoupling based on observational and statistical data, as well as multimodel simulations. Data on global, national, and regional water withdrawals indicate that certain peak water-use levels are being reached and the paper discusses past, current, and projected demand estimates; potential drivers of observed water use reductions; and different strategies for managing and modeling water use in the future. These findings indicate that the long-presumed correlation between water-resource use, economic development, and human well-being can be decoupled and that models of water use should reflect this. Decoupling solutions must focus on efficiency technologies, regulatory water-use caps, environmental flow protections, and enhanced monitoring networks.

title: Structural and Electronic Properties of Lead Halide Perovskite Thin-Film Surfaces
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Polycrystalline perovskite thin films are consistently associated with high-performance optoelectronic devices. The main challenges currently under the spotlight lie with the stability and reliability of these devices, requiring a better understanding of thin-film surfaces and interfaces. However, their consistent investigation is often very challenging. Given the soft nature of these materials, there is a struggle to directly assign the origin of the electronic features and correlate them to the chemical nature of the surfaces. Here, by exploiting a multimodal approach, we measure for the first time, at submicrometer scales, the diffraction patterns of the thin-film grain surface, which provide the material fingerprint and experimental evidence that the surface of such soft semiconductors is not as disordered as often claimed. Then, building on such knowledge, we move to ultraviolet photoemission spectroscopy, which provides information about the electronic structure of the first few nanometers of the thin-film surface. Having identified the structural nature of the surface, we are eventually able to unambiguously assign the origin of the photoemission spectra for a wide range of metal halide perovskites. In particular, metallic lead is identified to be the origin of the often-reported midgap photoemissive states, thus far assigned to deep electronic states within the halide perovskite semiconductor band gap. The chemical composition of the metal halides, the photodegradation of the perovskites under visible light, the quality of the precursors, and the actual stoichiometry of the thin film heavily define the presence of such states and elucidate the origin of carrier loss, photodegradation, and sample reproducibility in metal halide perovskite optoelectronics.

title: Redissolution Pathway Governed Solution-State and Crystallization Kinetics for Scalable Perovskite Photovoltaics
abstract: Although perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have achieved high efficiencies in small-area devices, uniform and controllable crystallization in large-area fabrication remained a key barrier to industrialization. In this work, we revealed...

title: Leptin Receptor + cells create a perisinusoidal niche for thrombopoiesis in the bone marrow by synthesizing CXCL14
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Leptin Receptor-expressing (LepR + ) stromal cells in the bone marrow are a critical source of growth factors for the maintenance of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) and most restricted hematopoietic progenitors. An important unresolved question is whether they also regulate terminal differentiation in some hematopoietic cells. We found that bone marrow LepR + cells promote thrombopoiesis by synthesizing the chemokine CXCL14. Cxcl14 -expressing LepR + cells extend fine processes that wrap around perisinusoidal megakaryocytes. Deletion of Cxcl14 from LepR + cells did not significantly alter HSC function or most aspects of bone marrow hematopoiesis, including megakaryocyte generation; however, it significantly reduced the numbers of proplatelet-forming megakaryocytes in the bone marrow and platelets in the blood, as well as platelet quality. Megakaryocytes from Lepr-cre; Cxcl14 fl/fl mice expressed lower levels of genes that encode granule proteins as compared to control mice, leading to the release of platelets with fewer α-granules and defective thrombus formation/growth. CXCL14 promoted platelet formation by remodeling lipid metabolism in megakaryocytes, increasing fatty acid transporter expression and enabling megakaryocytes to take up more polyunsaturated fatty acids from circulation. A high fat diet rescued the formation of proplatelet-forming megakaryocytes and platelets, as well as platelet function, in Lepr-cre; Cxcl14 fl/fl mice. CXCL14 protein was sufficient to promote platelet formation by megakaryocytes in vitro and in vivo. LepR + cells thus create a perisinusoidal niche for thrombopoiesis by producing CXCL14, which regulates lipid metabolism and terminal differentiation in megakaryocytes.

title: Vessel noise pollution offsets marine mammal energy budgets
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Shipping is a major global source of underwater noise pollution and is frequently reported to alter the behavior of marine mammals. However, the energetic consequences of these noise-induced behavioral disruptions and their implications for population fitness remain poorly quantified. Using behavioral proxies of energy acquisition and expenditure derived from high-resolution sound and movement tags on 28 wild harbor porpoises, we estimate that porpoises decrease energy acquisition by 20% (range: 1 to 36%) during high-noise vessel exposures, while maintaining constant energy expenditure. With a median of 11 high-noise vessel exposures per day, these disruptions may result in an average daily shortfall of 4.6% of their net energy budget. Sustained over time, such noise-induced energetic deficits have the potential to compromise individual fitness, ultimately affecting the dynamics of harbor porpoise populations in industrialized coastal areas worldwide and reducing their functional carrying capacity. This framework establishes a direct mechanistic link between behavioral disruption and fitness-relevant impacts, providing a biologically grounded metric for predicting population-level outcomes of noise pollution and an objective basis for defining acceptable exposure levels of vessel noise for wild marine mammal populations. Moreover, it is scalable across species and ecosystems and offers a common currency for assessing the cumulative effects of multiple stressors in the Anthropocene oceans. As vessel traffic and its associated noise outputs continue to increase globally, our results offer timely insights for evidence-based management, and support efforts to balance the societal demand for low-cost maritime transport with the responsibility to ensure the sustainable use and conservation of marine biodiversity.

title: Gaplinc regulates myeloid metabolic pathways in trans in endotoxic shock
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: The long noncoding RNA (lncRNA) Gaplinc is a known regulator of the innate immune response; however, the systemic mechanisms governing its influence on survival during endotoxic shock remain incompletely understood. Here, we establish Gaplinc as a dosage-dependent immune and metabolic rheostat. While Gaplinc knockout (KO) mice exhibit elevated baseline immune response genes (IRGs) and resistance to lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced shock, we demonstrate that transgenic Gaplinc overexpression produces the opposite phenotype: suppressed baseline IRGs, diminished nuclear p65, and hypersensitivity to endotoxemia. Analysis of heterozygous and rescue models reveals that Gaplinc functions in trans and is haploinsufficient, requiring strict transcript dosage to maintain wild-type immune homeostasis. To uncover the mechanistic basis of this survival advantage, we performed RNA Antisense Purification (RAP-MS) and identified the mitochondrial enzyme MCCC1 as a primary Gaplinc binding partner. Loss of Gaplinc drives systemic metabolic reprogramming, characterized by reduced mitochondrial reactive oxygen species and a protective lipidome featuring elevated lysophosphatidylcholines and diminished free fatty acids. Finally, while myeloid-specific conditional KOs confer partial protection against LPS-induced hypothermia, tissue-wide expression mapping and sex-dimorphic clinical chemistries suggest a broader, multisystemic role for the lncRNA. Collectively, these data demonstrate that Gaplinc bridges transcriptomic immune regulation with systemic lipid and metabolic output, dictating survival outcomes in systemic inflammation.

title: Chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan 4 participates in the internalization of arginine-rich dipeptide repeat proteins
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Microsatellite repeat expansion of the 5′ GGGGCC 3′ sequence in the C9orf72 gene is the most common monogenic form of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal dementia. Dipeptide repeat proteins (DPRs) translated from the mutant allele can be detected in postmortem brains of afflicted individuals. The arginine containing peptides, poly proline-arginine (poly-PR) and poly glycine-arginine (poly-GR), are particularly noxious to cells. Both can undergo cell-to-cell transmission, but underlying mechanisms are not understood. We found rapid internalization and nucleolar localization of bath-applied hemagglutinin (HA) tagged poly-PR with twenty repeats (HA-PR 20 ) in cell lines and neurons. Small molecule and RNAi approaches implicated a temperature-dependent, fluid phase endocytosis mechanism for HA-PR 20 . We sought to identify DPR-related cell surface uptake factors using µMap high-resolution proximity labeling. DPR–iridium conjugates identified candidate cell-surface proteins which were interrogated in a secondary RNAi screen. Focusing on our strongest candidate, chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan 4 (CSPG4), we showed cellular uptake of HA-PR 20 is reduced by inhibition of glycosaminoglycan chain synthesis and knockdown or ablation of CSPG4. Knockdown of CSPG4 protected PR 20 -induced neuronal toxicity. Using a dual reporter system to interrogate in vitro neuron-to-neuron transmission of PR 50, we found PR 50 synthesized by one neuron readily spread to neighboring cells. Transmission was significantly reduced with CSPG4 knockdown. Similarly conditioned media from PR 50 or GR 50 expressing neurons contained transmissible protein that was internalized into neurons in a CSPG4-dependent manner. These results suggest CSPG4 participates in poly-PR/poly-GR internalization and transmission.

title: Direct CO 2 splitting using light-based catalysis and an oxygen reservoir
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: As the dominant anthropogenic greenhouse gas, the conversion of CO 2 into value-added products is vital for achieving a circular economy. CO 2 activation typically requires coreactants, high temperatures, or significant electrical input, any of which increases cost or limits scalability. Here we demonstrate a straightforward way to split CO 2 directly into carbon monoxide and oxygen using light. By combining a light-driven antenna-reactor photocatalyst with a material that acts as an oxygen reservoir, CO 2 can be decomposed directly into CO and oxygen with light only. Under illumination, photoexcited carriers induce CO 2 bond dissociation, while cerium oxide adsorbs the released oxygen into vacancy sites, preventing recombination. The oxygen can then be released from the ceria by flowing nitrogen under white light illumination, a process that can be repeated multiple times, restoring full photocatalytic activity. This demonstrates a practical and scalable strategy for efficient CO 2 conversion, shifting the chemical equilibrium of CO 2 dissociation in a controllable manner.

title: Coupled human–cattle mobility shaped the socioeconomic landscapes of the Holocene Middle Nile Valley
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: We present a synthesis of strontium isotope data ( 87 Sr/ 86 Sr) from human and cattle dental enamel across Middle Nile. This dataset, which combines newly acquired and published measurements, reveals a complex history of human and cattle mobility linked to ecological gradients and sociocultural changes in this part of the continent. During the early Holocene (8,000 to 4,000 BCE), isotopic unanimity in human and cattle remains supports early, correlated mobility of humans and Bos , extending beyond Nile floodplains to adjacent uplands. In the mid-Holocene (4,000 to 1,000 BCE), isotopic data from Wadi Howar suggest bidirectional corridors for mobility of both species linking the Middle Nile and the Western Desert. This pattern correlates with the emergence of the Middle Nile civilizations in which cattle played a central cultural and economic role. From the first millennium BCE onward, a radical change can be observed, correlated with the progressive desertification processes in the Sahel. Although cattle import routes continued to follow wadi systems, they shifted south of the now desiccated Saharan lakes toward Kordofan. The long-term perspective emphasizes the continuous adaptation of societies in the Middle Nile of what is now Sudan and adjacent regions to environmental changes, aimed at maintaining sustained access to cattle, a resource that remained crucial for Middle Nile communities throughout the Holocene.

title: The broad-spectrum RumC1 bacteriocin targets a transient peptidoglycan intermediate of the nascent cell wall
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Ruminoccocin C1 (RumC1) is a structurally unique bacteriocin with broad-spectrum efficacy, including against multidrug-resistant pathogens, yet acting by an undefined mechanism. By integrating genetics, biochemistry, computational modeling, and single-cell fluorescence microscopy, we demonstrate that RumC1 is a distinct cell-wall-targeting toxin. First, all RumC1-resistant mutants isolated through a high-rate, genome-wide mutagenic screening exhibited specific impairments in peptidoglycan homeostasis regulation, pinpointing this pathway as critical for RumC1 activity. Second, RumC1 selectively accumulates within neosynthesized peptidoglycan, leading to cell growth arrest and death in a dose-dependent manner. Third, we characterize the RumI c 1 immunity protein of the RumC1 biosynthetic cluster as a peptidase acting at the cell surface to protect the cells by trimming the stem peptide crucial for cell-wall assembly. As such, RumI c 1 provides cross-protection against vancomycin, while RumC1 is demonstrated to act differently from this glycopeptide antibiotic. Collectively, these findings establish RumC1 as a toxin targeting a key peptidoglycan intermediate of cell wall maturation, which defines a distinct mode of action among the large and highly diverse repertoire of bacteriocins characterized so far.

title: Global lake synchrony signals rising planetary-scale ecological coupling
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Understanding how localized ecosystem dynamics scale up to influence Earth-system stability remains a major challenge. Lakes, though covering less than 2% of Earth’s surface, play a disproportionate role in regulating global carbon, nutrient, and biodiversity dynamics, making them a critical nexus for assessing emerging large-scale environmental coupling. By integrating satellite observations with century-scale sedimentary archives from ~2,000 lakes, we reveal a marked acceleration in global lake synchrony since 2000. This synchronization, coinciding with converging climatic and socioeconomic pressures, signals a widespread erosion of the spatial heterogeneity and regional distinctiveness that historically characterized inland waters. We propose that increasing lake synchrony represents an emergent property of the Anthropocene, transforming lakes from regionally structured, asynchronous waterscapes into dynamically coupled planetary commons. By temporally aligning carbon and nutrient dynamics across broad spatial scales, this synchronization modifies the timing and amplitude of aggregate biophysical fluxes, altering how inland waters interact with larger-scale environmental cycles. Ultimately, this finding motivates a macroscale monitoring framework that jointly tracks synchrony, modularity, and their functional consequences, demanding a shift in governance toward preserving the ecological heterogeneity essential for maintaining long-term environmental stability.

title: Automating inequality? Gender bias in AI-mediated labor markets
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Generative AI is rapidly entering labor markets, with large language models (LLMs) now used to help write CVs and evaluate applicants. We study the risks this creates in a series of audit experiments in which applicant gender is randomly assigned while all other information is held constant. We find that LLMs generate gender-stereotypical CVs and exhibit gender bias in screening scores and wage recommendations. Screening scores track occupational gender segregation, penalizing women in male-dominated occupations and favoring them in female-dominated ones. Wage recommendations track occupational gender wage gaps when gender is explicit in the prompt, though this gradient weakens under name-based gender signaling and is sensitive to the LLMs being used. These disparities arise through two channels: evaluation bias, when identical CV content is evaluated differently by gender, and generation bias, when gendered content produced by the model affects later evaluation. Because the same systems shape both CV content and its subsequent assessment, these channels can reinforce one another. Taken together, our findings identify measurable risks of algorithmic amplification in AI-mediated job search.

title: Stature reveals changing patterns of the biological standard of living in Europe and Asia over the past 7,000 y
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
